info.title: Distyra Transaction Enrichment API
info.description:
EU-native PSD2-specialist transaction enrichment.

Authenticate every request with a bearer API key (`Authorization: Bearer sk_…`).
Errors share a common shape: `{ error: string, detail?: string }`.

**Idempotency.** Set an `Idempotency-Key` header on POST requests to make retries safe. 
The first response is cached for 24h keyed by (organization, route, key); subsequent 
requests with the same key replay the cached response and add `Idempotent-Replay: true`. 
Reusing a key with a different request body returns 422 `idempotency_key_reused_with_different_body`. Use a fresh key for a different operation. 
Idempotency deduplicates retries, not concurrent races.

Confidence values are uncalibrated similarity scores, not probabilities of correctness; treat them as relative signals, not absolute.

**Base URL.** `https://api.distyra.com`. The API and CDN stay on `.com`; only the Distyra website uses `.eu`.

**Versioning.** The API is versioned in the path (`/v1`). `/v1` is **stable**: an 
improvement arrives as something you choose to use, such as a new endpoint, a new response 
field or a new optional request parameter, and nothing an existing integration relies on is 
removed, renamed or changes meaning. A breaking change ships as a new version (`/v2`), and 
`/v1` keeps working for at least 12 months after it is announced. During that window, the 
calls that use the deprecated operation or field carry a `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745, for 
example `Deprecation: @1798761600`), a `Sunset` header with the date after which they may 
stop working (RFC 8594), and a `Link` to the migration notes. Both SDKs print a warning when 
they see them. The change is announced in the changelog. Organizations whose traffic uses it 
are emailed when it is announced and again before the sunset date.

Build a **tolerant reader**: ignore response fields you do not know, and do not hard-fail 
on an unknown enum value or error code. New endpoints, new optional request fields, new 
response fields, new values in an open-ended enum (a new `category.source`, a new statement 
format, a new error `code`), new optional response headers and relaxed validation all ship 
in `/v1` without notice.

**Two exceptions, both in effect on the day they ship.** The first runs in your favour: a 
change that stops us returning or holding 
personal data we have no need for ships in `/v1` even when it is technically breaking, 
because waiting for a `/v2` would mean over-sharing for the length of a deprecation window. 
It is a narrow door: the change is announced in the changelog on the day it ships with the 
reason, affected organizations are emailed, and where the data is genuinely still needed a 
reduced form replaces it rather than the field simply vanishing, so the shape of your 
integration survives. The second is a suspension of part of the service that legal or 
regulatory reasons require. It is announced in the changelog on the day it takes effect, and 
the organizations it affects are emailed.

**Rate limits.** Two windows, both keyed on your organization, both enforced on 
every authenticated route:

| Plan | Sustained (per 60s window) | Burst (per 1s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Developer | 5 req/s | 20 req/s |
| Growth | 50 req/s | 200 req/s |
| Enterprise | 1,000 req/s | 5,000 req/s |

Batch routes additionally spend a per-minute *item* budget (20,000 items/min on 
Developer, 200,000 on Growth), so one 100-item batch costs 100 items, not 1. 
Exceeding either window returns 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` (seconds) 
and the `x-ratelimit-limit` / `x-ratelimit-remaining` / `x-ratelimit-reset` 
headers. The 429 body also carries `scope` (which window tripped), 
`retry_after_seconds` and `max`, so a retry policy need not parse headers. 
Per-organization overrides are available on request.

**Test-mode keys are always held to the Developer limits above**, whatever your 
plan and whatever per-organization override is in place. They also count in 
their own bucket, so test traffic can never consume your live allowance (or the 
other way round). Load-test against a live key.

**Webhook signatures.** Every delivery carries 
`X-Distyra-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac_sha256_hex>`. The HMAC input is the 
literal string `<unix>.<raw_body>`. Sign the raw body, before any JSON 
re-serialization, keyed with the endpoint's signing secret. Compare in 
constant time, and reject timestamps older than your tolerance (we recommend 
300 seconds) to stop replays. During a secret rotation both secrets sign the 
same delivery and the header carries two tags (`v1=<old>,v2=<new>`); accept a 
match on either until you have cut over. `verifyWebhook` in `@distyra/sdk` and 
`distyra` implements this. Delivery envelope and retry schedule: see the 
`WebhookDelivery` schema.

**Error codes.** The `error` field is one of:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `missing_authorization` | No bearer token was supplied in the Authorization header. |
| `invalid_key` | The API key is missing, malformed, revoked, or expired. |
| `unauthorized` | The request is not authorized. |
| `insufficient_scope` | The API key lacks a scope required for this operation. |
| `invalid_act_as_org` | The service principal named an act-as organization it may not act for. |
| `invalid_act_as_env` | A service-principal call named an environment other than live or sandbox. |
| `service_missing_act_as_org` | A service-principal call omitted the required act-as organization. |
| `test_mode_unsupported` | This operation cannot be performed with a test-mode (sk_test_) key. |
| `insufficient_credit` | The organization has no funded balance to cover this charge. Top up to continue. |
| `developer_quota_exceeded` | The free developer-tier monthly quota is exhausted. Upgrade or top up. |
| `suspended` | The organization is suspended (typically for non-payment). |
| `account_deletion_pending` | The organization's deletion has been requested; its bank connections are ended and their data cannot be read. |
| `deletion_not_requested` | The operation applies only to an organization whose deletion has been requested. |
| `payment_disputed` | A payment dispute (chargeback) on this account is open, so nothing new can be charged. Free and already-paid usage keeps working. |
| `plan_upgrade_required` | The current plan does not include this feature; upgrade to use it. |
| `no_underwriting_subscription` | Underwriting is not enabled for this organization (sales-led). |
| `connect_mode_unavailable` | This Connect mode is not available for your organization at the moment. Contact support@distyra.eu for more information. |
| `business_verification_required` | Live mode 'end_user' connections are available to verified businesses, and this organization is not verified. The detail says what would verify it. |
| `business_verification_pending` | This organization's business verification is in progress (an EU VAT number check or a review). Live mode 'end_user' connections open once it completes. |
| `sales_led_only` | This endpoint is sales-led and gated behind a contract flag. |
| `consumer_underwriting_not_entitled` | This organization is not contracted for consumer (natural-person) underwriting. applicant_type=consumer requires a separate contractual scope with its own data-processing schedule. |
| `household_business_applicant` | household was supplied with applicant_type=business. It is echoed on the consumer affordability feature, which does not exist on the business profile, so it would be accepted and never used. Refused rather than ignored, and also because household composition is personal data about people who are not the applicant: accepting it on a path with no use for it is a minimisation problem before it is an API-design one. |
| `declared_income_business_applicant` | declared_monthly_income was supplied with applicant_type=business. It engages income corroboration, which is a consumer feature, so there is nothing for it to corroborate. Refused rather than ignored: a supplied figure that silently does nothing is worse than a refusal. |
| `balance_unavailable` | The balance could not be read to authorize the charge; retry shortly. |
| `spend_cap_reached` | The organization reached its self-serve monthly spend cap. Raise or remove the cap in Billing settings to continue. |
| `rate_limited` | Too many requests. The per-organization rate limit was exceeded. Retry after the window. |
| `invalid_idempotency_key` | The Idempotency-Key header is malformed. |
| `idempotency_key_reused_with_different_body` | The idempotency key was reused with a different request body. |
| `validation_failed` | The request failed schema validation (see detail). |
| `invalid_request` | The request is malformed or missing required fields. |
| `invalid_meta` | The supplied metadata object is invalid. |
| `missing_meta` | A required metadata field was not supplied. |
| `invalid_list` | The supplied list value is invalid. |
| `invalid_email` | The supplied email address is invalid. |
| `invalid_country` | The supplied country code is invalid or unsupported. |
| `invalid_cursor` | The pagination cursor is malformed or expired. |
| `invalid_expires_before` | The supplied expires_before is not an ISO 8601 date-time. |
| `invalid_history` | history or enrich_history was combined with a parameter it cannot be used with: history with date_from, since or a past date_to, or enrich_history without enrich=true. |
| `mode_requires_applicant_ref` | mode 'applicant' was requested without an applicant_ref. |
| `mode_conflicts_with_applicant_ref` | The requested mode and applicant_ref describe different account holders. |
| `return_url_required` | mode 'end_user' needs a return_url so the account holder lands back in your product. |
| `invalid_return_url` | The supplied return URL is invalid or not allow-listed. |
| `brand_logo_url_unsupported` | A hosted link cannot carry its own logo; upload it under Connect branding in the portal. |
| `unsupported_window` | The requested time window is not supported. |
| `unsupported` | The requested operation or option is not supported. |
| `item_failed` | An individual item in a batch could not be processed (per-item, non-fatal). |
| `not_found` | The requested resource was not found. |
| `account_not_found` | The referenced account was not found. |
| `analysis_not_found` | The referenced underwriting analysis was not found. |
| `ingestion_not_found` | The referenced statement ingestion was not found. |
| `invoice_not_found` | The referenced invoice was not found. |
| `payment_not_found` | The referenced payment was not found. |
| `payment_not_refundable` | The payment cannot be refunded: it is not paid, or nothing is left on it. |
| `refund_exceeds_refundable` | The refund is more than the unused prepaid balance after what is due. |
| `refund_override_not_allowed` | Only the admin can refund above the refundable balance. |
| `service_principal_only` | This operation is available to Distyra first-party services only. |
| `no_file` | No file was supplied in the upload. |
| `no_files` | No files were supplied in the upload. |
| `missing_file` | A required file part was missing from the multipart upload. |
| `empty_file` | The uploaded file was empty. |
| `file_too_large` | The uploaded file exceeds the size limit. |
| `too_large` | The request payload exceeds the size limit. |
| `unsupported_media_type` | The request content type is not supported. |
| `unsupported_format` | The statement file format is not supported. |
| `format_mismatch` | The declared format does not match the file contents. |
| `mixed_formats` | A multi-file upload mixed incompatible statement formats. |
| `conflict_currency_mix` | The uploaded statements mix currencies in a way that cannot be reconciled. |
| `no_accounts` | No accounts were found in the uploaded statement. |
| `no_accounts_parsed` | No accounts could be parsed from the uploaded statement. |
| `no_eur_accounts` | No EUR-denominated accounts were found in the statement. |
| `no_usable_entries` | No usable transaction entries were found in the statement. |
| `no_staged_files` | No staged files are available for this operation. |
| `no_statement_evidence` | No statement evidence was supplied to support the analysis. |
| `invalid_account_data` | The supplied account data is invalid. |
| `invalid_parsed_account` | A parsed account failed validation. |
| `too_many_accounts` | The upload contains more accounts than allowed. |
| `too_many_files` | The upload contains more files than allowed. |
| `too_many_transactions` | The upload contains more transactions than allowed. |
| `too_many_staged_files` | More staged files than allowed for this operation. |
| `staged_bundle_too_large` | The staged file bundle exceeds the size limit. |
| `staged_file_expired` | A staged file has expired and must be re-uploaded. |
| `partial_parse_rejected` | The statement parsed only partially and was rejected. |
| `async_pdf_only` | PDF statements must be processed via the asynchronous endpoint. |
| `pdf_pending` | The PDF is still being parsed asynchronously; retry later. |
| `pdf_unavailable` | The PDF parser is temporarily unavailable. |
| `pdf_extraction_unreliable` | PDF text extraction was too unreliable to use. |
| `analysis_purged` | The analysis has passed its retention window and was purged. |
| `ingestion_purged` | The ingestion has passed its retention window and was purged. |
| `connect_unconfigured` | Connect is not configured for this organization. |
| `connect_sandbox_unconfigured` | Connect sandbox is not configured. |
| `connection_not_active` | The bank connection is not active. |
| `connection_not_pending` | A revoke sent with `expected_status=pending` found the connection already authorized (`active`), or authorized and since lapsed (`expired`). Nothing was changed. Not the inverse of `connection_not_active`: that one refuses to **read** a connection that is not usable, this one refuses to **end** one that is. |
| `consent_expired` | The bank-data consent has expired and must be renewed. |
| `bank_fetch_limit_reached` | This connection has used its daily allowance of unattended bank fetches, counting attempts that failed. We apply the PSD2 limit on unattended access (RTS 2018/389 Art. 36(5)(b)), and a bank may apply it too; it is not a limit on the account. `resets_at` is the next UTC midnight, and a fetch made while the end user is on screen does not count. |
| `bank_unavailable` | The bank did not answer the last request for this connection, so automated fetches for it are paused for a few minutes. Nothing was sent to the bank and no daily fetch was used; retry after `retry_after_seconds`. A fetch made while the end user is on screen is not paused. |
| `unknown_aspsp` | The requested bank (ASPSP) is not recognized. |
| `link_expired` | The hosted link has expired. |
| `link_not_active` | The hosted link is not active. |
| `invalid_or_expired` | The token or link is invalid or expired. |
| `mollie_not_configured` | The payment provider is not configured. |
| `mollie_unavailable` | The payment provider is temporarily unavailable. |
| `webhook_endpoint_limit` | The maximum number of webhook endpoints for this organization was reached. |
| `storage_unavailable` | Object storage is temporarily unavailable; retry shortly. |
| `upstream_error` | An upstream dependency returned an error. |
| `activation_failed` | Activation could not be completed. |
| `rotation_failed` | API key rotation could not be completed. |
| `internal_error` | An unexpected server error occurred. Quote request_id when contacting support. |
| `service_unavailable` | A dependency is temporarily unavailable; retry shortly. |

WebhookDelivery.description:
The body POSTed to a registered webhook endpoint.

**Discriminator.** Enrichment batch events name themselves in an `event` field;
every other event uses `type`. That split is historical and is part of the wire
contract, so read whichever your subscription implies rather than assuming one.

**Test and live.** An endpoint has the mode of the key that created it, and receives
only events about activity in that mode: an endpoint created with a test key hears
about sandbox connections, one created with a live key about real ones. Every
delivery carries `livemode` so a handler can check rather than trust the routing.

**Delivery and retries.** One POST per (endpoint, event), 10s timeout. Any
non-2xx is retried up to 6 times, so 7 attempts in all,
at +1m, +5m, +30m, +2h, +6h and +24h after each failure:
about 33 hours from the first attempt to the last. Every failed attempt counts toward the
consecutive failures that disable an endpoint (below), so an endpoint that is down reaches
that limit after fewer deliveries than attempts suggest.
Respond 2xx as soon as you have durably accepted the payload and do the work
afterwards. Delivery is at-least-once: a timeout after your handler
committed still retries, so key your processing on the id in the payload. Deliveries are
not ordered: two events about the same connection can arrive in either order.
After 20 consecutive failures the endpoint is disabled automatically and must
be re-enabled via PATCH /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}.

**Verification.** See `X-Distyra-Signature` under Webhook signatures above.
Verify before trusting the body; an unverified delivery is an unauthenticated
POST from the internet.

event.description: Present on enrichment batch deliveries only. Names the event.

type.description: Present on every non-batch delivery. Names the event.

livemode.description: Every delivery. `false` when the event is about test-mode activity (a batch submitted, or a connection created, with a test key), which only reaches endpoints created with a test key.

batch_id.description: `batch.*` only. The async batch. Fetch the result from GET /v1/enrich/batch/async/{id} within 24h of submission.

status_url.description: `batch.completed` only. Path to the batch result.

external_ref.description: `connect.connection.*` only. Your own reference, echoed back.

applicant_ref.description: `connect.connection.*` only. Your own applicant reference, echoed back.

mode.description: `connect.connection.*` only. Whose account this is: `own` (your organization's), `applicant` (your underwriting applicant's), or `end_user` (the end user of an application you offer). Read this rather than inferring from whether `applicant_ref` is set, which cannot tell `own` and `end_user` apart.

days_left.description: `connect.connection.reconsent_required` only. Days until the consent expires.

reason.description:
`connect.connection.error`: why the connection attempt failed.

`connect.connection.revoked`: who ended it. `customer_request` (an API DELETE, or the account holder using a revoke link you minted), `past_due` (we ended it because the balance stayed unpaid past the grace window, so every connection on that organization is ending), `abandoned` (the account holder never finished authorizing), `superseded` (the same account holder re-authorized at this bank and a new connection replaced this one; the feed continues under the new id, and this is the only revoke reason where data keeps flowing), `ended_at_bank` (the bank reports the consent is over, most often because the account holder withdrew it in their banking app; ask them to reconnect), or `account_deleted` (your organization asked to delete its Distyra account, which ends every connection that day).

failure_kind.description: `connect.connection.error` only. The more specific account of the failure that `failure_kind` gives on GET /v1/connect/connections/{id}, with the same values (`bank_error`, `authorization_rejected`, `authorization_failed` and the rest), beside an unchanged `reason`. An open enum: keep a default branch.

error.description: `batch.failed` only. Terminal reason.

get.summary: List the banks (ASPSPs) Connect covers across Europe
get.description:
The banks Distyra Connect can connect to for business accounts, and how many there are per country. This is the list the coverage page on distyra.eu is built from.

**Public:** no API key is needed. The list is always the live one, whichever key mode you use elsewhere.

**Freshness:** the list is cached for up to 24 hours and refreshed in the background once it is older than that, so `updated_at` says how old the answer is. The response carries `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`.

**Errors:** 503 `connect_unconfigured` while Connect is not configured; 502 `upstream_error` when the list cannot be fetched from Enable Banking and nothing is cached yet.

updated_at.description: When this list was fetched from Enable Banking.

name.description: The bank name as Enable Banking lists it.

post.summary: Enrich a single transaction
post.description:
Single-transaction enrichment. Returns the full response shape with an `availability` block. In that block `merchant_identity`, `transaction_type` and `logos` are constants meaning the feature has shipped, while `location` and `subscription_detection` report whether this request had the data the field needs. `metadata.is_subscription` is a merchant-category hint, not per-transaction recurrence, and is null when no merchant resolved. Confidence values are uncalibrated similarity scores.

**Our AI provider.** To identify a merchant, or to check that a merchant we identified matches the transaction, we may send the transaction to our AI provider, an EU sub-processor under a zero-retention, no-training agreement, together with its amount, currency, MCC and country. `cache_only=true` prevents this.

**Required scope:** `enrichment:read`.

descriptor.description: Raw bank descriptor as it appeared on the statement. Required.

amount.description: Transaction amount. Negative = debit, positive = credit. Optional; it can help with transactions we cannot resolve from the description alone.

mcc.description: Merchant Category Code (4-digit ISO 18245). Optional; like amount, it can help with transactions we cannot resolve from the description alone.

country_hint.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code. Helps tell apart merchants that share a name in different countries.

merchant_name.description: Pre-cleaned merchant name, if you already have one from your own processing.

bank_code_description.description: Provider-supplied transaction-code label (e.g. SEPA RCT, ATM withdrawal).

parameters.name: force_refresh
parameters.description: When `true`, do not reuse an earlier answer for this descriptor: work it out again, and keep the new answer for later requests. If it resolves to a merchant, that merchant's logo and details are refreshed in the background. Mutually exclusive with `cache_only=true`.

parameters.name: min_confidence
parameters.description: Filter ready responses by `confidence_bucket`. When set and the result's `confidence_bucket` is below the threshold (e.g. result=`low` with `min_confidence=high`), the response still includes the merchant block but with `meets_min_confidence: false`. Callers can either skip the result or relax the threshold and retry.

parameters.name: cache_only
parameters.description: When `true`, we answer only from what we already know, and the call never sends data to our AI provider. Mutually exclusive with `force_refresh=true`.

parameters.name: wait_for_crawl
parameters.description: When `true` and the merchant is new to us, wait up to `wait_timeout_ms` for its logo to be found, then return it instead of `logo_url: null`. No effect for merchants we already know. On timeout, returns the normal response, which carries a lower-quality favicon when one is available.

parameters.name: wait_timeout_ms
parameters.description: Upper bound in milliseconds for `wait_for_crawl` (default 8000, max 15000). Ignored unless `wait_for_crawl=true`.

source.description: How `merchant.name` was arrived at. **`descriptor` is the one value to branch on**: it means nothing was identified and `name` is your own descriptor handed back, tidied where we could, so the transaction still has something to render. It always comes with `availability.merchant_identity: false`, a null `catalog_id` and a null `confidence_bucket`; treat it as unenriched and do not store it as a merchant identity. **The other four all mean a merchant was identified**, and differ only in how: `catalog` a merchant from our curated catalogue, `crawl` a merchant identified from public sources, `fuzzy_match` a catalogue merchant whose name is close to but not exactly the one we saw, `llm_inferred` a name proposed by an AI model. Read `confidence_bucket` rather than ranking those four: they say how the answer was reached, not how good it is. `null` means no merchant block was served to describe. Treat the set as open and keep a default branch.

category.description: Category labels for the resolved merchant. When the merchant is in our catalogue, `primary` is always its catalogue industry (even if null), so the label is stable however the merchant was identified. Labels proposed by an AI model appear only for a merchant not in our catalogue, marked `source: "llm"`.

source.description: Where the category labels came from. 'catalog': the curated catalog row's industry/subindustry (deterministic: the same merchant always returns the same category). 'llm': labels proposed by an AI model for a merchant not yet in our catalogue, drawn from the same vocabulary but not yet reviewed by us. null: no category available.

is_subscription.description: Merchant-category hint: true when the resolved merchant predominantly bills on subscription (streaming, SaaS, telco, gym, insurance). This reflects the merchant, not this transaction: a single charge at a subscription merchant may still be a one-off. True only for conservatively curated brands. Null means no merchant resolved, so there was no catalog row to consult; false means a row resolved and is not on the curated list. Before 2026-07-16 the unresolved case also reported false, which asserted a negative we had no basis for. Per-account recurrence detection needs the transaction series and lives in the banking/iOS layer, not this stateless API.

transaction_type.description: bank_fee | internal_transfer | p2p_transfer | cash_withdrawal | cash_deposit | investment_transfer | salary | refund | direct_debit | standing_order | returned_dd | merchant_payment. "merchant_payment" is the ordinary-purchase verdict: no other transaction type applied, and a merchant or category was identified, so this is a normal payment to a business. Null means genuinely undetermined (nothing resolved). Before 2026-07-16 ordinary purchases reported null at confidence 0, indistinguishable from "no idea", while the docs advertised a "merchant_payment" value that was not in the enum and could never be returned.

country_matching.description: Whether country-constrained matching was available for this request. It describes the request rather than the answer, and that distinction is the point: `constrained` reflects the `country_hint` you sent, not a country inferred from the descriptor text. A descriptor ending in a country code may still constrain matching while this reads false, because the advice being given is about what your integration can change. Why it exists: without a country, a same-named merchant in another country can win, and nothing used to say so. A German consumer statement sent with no hint resolved to .fi, .at, .ie, .pl and .nl domains. It is returned on both paths, so a client can read it unconditionally.

constrained.description: True when this request supplied `country_hint`, so matching could prefer a merchant in that country over a same-named one elsewhere. False when it did not.

advisory.description: A sentence when `constrained` is false, null when it is true. Read the boolean rather than testing whether this object is present, because the object is returned on every response.

type_unavailable.description:
Why `transaction_type` is null, or null when a type was determined. A bare null type is indistinguishable from "we tried and failed", and the two need different responses from you. 

Each reason describes this transaction, not your bank in general. One row without a transaction code does not establish that a bank never sends them, so aggregate across many transactions before concluding anything about an institution.

reason.description: transient_failure: enrichment failed transiently; see `resolution` and retry. bank_sent_no_type_data: we read this transaction from the bank and it carried no transaction code of any kind, neither a text description nor a structured ISO 20022 or proprietary code, and no MCC, so there was nothing to determine a type from. no_type_data_supplied: you sent neither bank_code_description nor mcc and we did not read the record ourselves, so we cannot tell whether your bank provides them. Where your bank provides a bank_code_description, sending it is the most reliable way to get a type. bank_code_unrecognised: a transaction code reached us, from you or from the bank record itself, and we do not decode it yet. That is our gap, not your bank's; tell us the code and we will add it. no_rule_matched: the transaction carried type information we understood, but it did not establish a type, and no merchant or category was identified.

retryable.description: True only for transient_failure. Every other reason is a settled answer for this transaction.

counterparty_role.description:
**What this counterparty is to the account holder**, when the resolved catalog row is tagged. Null when it is not, which is the common case: tagging is curated per row and ordinary merchants are deliberately untagged.

**Null does not mean "not one of these".** It means we hold no curated claim either way, and the two should not be presented the same way to anyone making a decision.

Carried over from the business profile: `tax_authority` a tax or revenue body, refined by `statutory_kind` when it is really a social-charge body; `lender` a credit provider, excluding mortgages which are separate below; `internal_transfer` another account of the holder's own.

Business-side: `customer` pays the holder for goods or services; `supplier` is paid by them for the same; `payment_processor` settles card or platform takings, so money arriving from one is usually revenue that has already been earned; `employee` is paid wages by the holder.

Consumer-side, added 2026-08-12: `employer` pays the holder wages, the inverse of `employee`, and the direction is the whole meaning; `benefits_agency` pays state benefits, kept separate from `employer` because some lenders may not count benefits toward affordability; `pension_provider`; `landlord`; `mortgage_provider`, separate from `lender` because housing cost is treated differently from unsecured credit in every market we surveyed; `utility`; `insurer`; `childcare`; `alimony_recipient`; `education`.

**No value here names a health condition, a religion, a political opinion or any other GDPR Article 9 special category**, and none will be added that does. That is a deliberate property rather than a coincidence: it is what lets a transaction suppressed as special-category keep its role, and `benefits_agency` names a payer rather than a reason for payment for the same reason.

**Five of the seventeen have catalog rows today** (measured 2026-10-06: `tax_authority` 159, `lender` 74, `payment_processor` 21, `benefits_agency` 8, `mortgage_provider` 4). The other twelve are published and currently return for nothing. They are listed because the vocabulary is the contract and a value appearing later must not be a surprise, not because coverage is implied.

**Treat it as an open enum**: switch on what you know and keep a default branch. A new role ships in `/v1` without a version bump; a role is never **removed** from it in place.

statutory_kind.description:
Refines a `counterparty_role` of `tax_authority` into **which statutory charge** it collects, so a social contribution is not reported as general taxation. Null on every other role, and null on a tax authority we hold no refinement for.

`social_security` a general social-insurance body; `health` a health-insurance contribution; `pension` a state or mandatory occupational scheme; `accident` statutory accident or injury insurance; `sectoral` an industry-specific mandatory fund; `social_secretariat` an intermediary that collects on a body's behalf, which is a payee rather than the charge itself; `other` a statutory charge that is none of the above.

**It names the charge, not a condition.** `health` is a health-insurance contribution that nearly everyone in the relevant country pays; it says nothing about the account holder's health and is not a GDPR Article 9 special category. Curated per row, not inferred from the industry taxonomy, which collapsed the statutory subindustries into broad ones shared with commercial entities in June 2026.

**Treat it as an open enum**, as with `counterparty_role`.

resolution.description: Structured reason for the resolution outcome, so callers can act on null results.

status.description: resolved: a merchant or non-merchant transaction_type was resolved. unresolved_unknown: we could not identify the merchant. low_signal_descriptor: the descriptor was too thin to resolve, so send the fuller statement form. below_mint_threshold: we found a possible merchant name, but not with enough confidence to report it as identified (see proposed_name/confidence). timed_out / transient_error: a transient failure during identification. Retryable, not a verdict. rate_limited: merchant identification is paused by a safeguard, so this response carries a cleaned descriptor without a newly identified merchant. The request itself still succeeds with 200. Retryable: retry_after gives the seconds until it clears, and message a sentence you can show a user. Ordinary use does not reach it, and sustained request rates are governed separately and answer 429.

retryable.description: true for timed_out / transient_error / rate_limited. Retry the same request; the null is transient, not a definitive "unknown". When retry_after is set, wait that long first.

retry_after.description: Seconds after which retrying the same descriptor is worthwhile, or null when it is not. Set when an unknown merchant triggered background discovery: the system is fetching + confirming the brand, so the descriptor typically resolves after this delay (eventual consistency). Also set on rate_limited, where it is the seconds until the protective limit clears and retrying before it will hit the same thing. Retry once after this many seconds, or just let your next natural re-sync pick it up. null = a definitive non-result, no retry will help.

message.description: A short human-readable sentence you can surface to a user, or null. Populated only where `status` alone cannot convey what to do about it: today that is rate_limited, where it says what is degraded and how long for. `status` remains the machine-readable contract; do not branch on this string.

cache_tier.description: An opaque indicator of how this answer was produced. **It is not a quality, accuracy, or confidence signal and its values carry no ordering**: a higher number is not a better answer. **Do not branch on it.** To tell whether a merchant was identified, read availability.merchant_identity or merchant.source; for confidence, read confidence.merchant or merchant.confidence_bucket.

availability.description: Per-request summary of what this one response actually yielded. Changed in 0.8.0: merchant_identity/transaction_type/logos used to be build-time constants meaning "the feature has shipped", hardcoded true on every response, which contradicted the payload (merchant_identity:true beside merchant.name:null). They now report what you actually got. Changed in 0.9.0: merchant_identity is no longer equivalent to `merchant.name !== null`. When nothing resolves, merchant.name now carries your own descriptor back (merchant.source = "descriptor") so the transaction still has something to display, and merchant_identity stays false. merchant_identity.description: **True when a merchant was identified**, whether one already in our catalogue or one newly proposed. **Not the same as merchant.name being populated.** When nothing resolves, merchant.name carries your own descriptor back (merchant.source = "descriptor") and this stays false.

transaction_type.description: True when metadata.transaction_type is populated. Distinct from merchant_identity: a bank fee can be typed with no merchant identified.

logos.description: True when merchant.logo_url is populated on this response.

location.description: True when this descriptor yielded a city or country.

subscription_detection.description: True when a catalog row resolved, so its subscription flag was available to consult. Equivalently, metadata.is_subscription is not null.

livemode.description: true when served to a live key; false when served to a test-mode (sk_test_) key. Test-mode responses are enriched the same way but carry no billing or quota impact.

post.summary: Enrich a batch of transactions
post.description:
Batch enrichment of up to 100 items per call. Items run with concurrency 10. Per-item failures surface as `{ error, detail }` in the corresponding result slot; one bad row never fails the batch. Larger jobs (>100) use the async batch endpoint. Query-string flags (`force_refresh`, `min_confidence`, `cache_only`) apply to every item in the batch.

**Our AI provider.** To identify a merchant, or to check that a merchant we identified matches the transaction, we may send the transaction to our AI provider, an EU sub-processor under a zero-retention, no-training agreement, together with its amount, currency, MCC and country. `cache_only=true` prevents this.

**Required scope:** `enrichment:read`.

descriptor.description: Raw bank descriptor as it appeared on the statement. Required.

amount.description: Transaction amount. Negative = debit, positive = credit. Optional; it can help with transactions we cannot resolve from the description alone.

mcc.description: Merchant Category Code (4-digit ISO 18245). Optional; like amount, it can help with transactions we cannot resolve from the description alone.

country_hint.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code. Helps tell apart merchants that share a name in different countries.

merchant_name.description: Pre-cleaned merchant name, if you already have one from your own processing.

bank_code_description.description: Provider-supplied transaction-code label (e.g. SEPA RCT, ATM withdrawal).

parameters.name: cache_only

**Treat it as an open enum**: switch on what you know and keep a default branch. A new role ships in `/v1` without a version bump; a role is never **removed** from it in place.

statutory_kind.description:
Refines a `counterparty_role` of `tax_authority` into **which statutory charge** it collects, so a social contribution is not reported as general taxation. Null on every other role, and null on a tax authority we hold no refinement for.

`social_security` a general social-insurance body; `health` a health-insurance contribution; `pension` a state or mandatory occupational scheme; `accident` statutory accident or injury insurance; `sectoral` an industry-specific mandatory fund; `social_secretariat` an intermediary that collects on a body's behalf, which is a payee rather than the charge itself; `other` a statutory charge that is none of the above.

**It names the charge, not a condition.** `health` is a health-insurance contribution that nearly everyone in the relevant country pays; it says nothing about the account holder's health and is not a GDPR Article 9 special category. Curated per row, not inferred from the industry taxonomy, which collapsed the statutory subindustries into broad ones shared with commercial entities in June 2026.

**Treat it as an open enum**, as with `counterparty_role`.

resolution.description: Structured reason for the resolution outcome, so callers can act on null results.

status.description: resolved: a merchant or non-merchant transaction_type was resolved. unresolved_unknown: we could not identify the merchant. low_signal_descriptor: the descriptor was too thin to resolve, so send the fuller statement form. below_mint_threshold: we found a possible merchant name, but not with enough confidence to report it as identified (see proposed_name/confidence). timed_out / transient_error: a transient failure during identification. Retryable, not a verdict. rate_limited: merchant identification is paused by a safeguard, so this response carries a cleaned descriptor without a newly identified merchant. The request itself still succeeds with 200. Retryable: retry_after gives the seconds until it clears, and message a sentence you can show a user. Ordinary use does not reach it, and sustained request rates are governed separately and answer 429.

retryable.description: true for timed_out / transient_error / rate_limited. Retry the same request; the null is transient, not a definitive "unknown". When retry_after is set, wait that long first.

retry_after.description: Seconds after which retrying the same descriptor is worthwhile, or null when it is not. Set when an unknown merchant triggered background discovery: the system is fetching + confirming the brand, so the descriptor typically resolves after this delay (eventual consistency). Also set on rate_limited, where it is the seconds until the protective limit clears and retrying before it will hit the same thing. Retry once after this many seconds, or just let your next natural re-sync pick it up. null = a definitive non-result, no retry will help.

message.description: A short human-readable sentence you can surface to a user, or null. Populated only where `status` alone cannot convey what to do about it: today that is rate_limited, where it says what is degraded and how long for. `status` remains the machine-readable contract; do not branch on this string.

cache_tier.description: An opaque indicator of how this answer was produced. **It is not a quality, accuracy, or confidence signal and its values carry no ordering**: a higher number is not a better answer. **Do not branch on it.** To tell whether a merchant was identified, read availability.merchant_identity or merchant.source; for confidence, read confidence.merchant or merchant.confidence_bucket.

availability.description: Per-request summary of what this one response actually yielded. Changed in 0.8.0: merchant_identity/transaction_type/logos used to be build-time constants meaning "the feature has shipped", hardcoded true on every response, which contradicted the payload (merchant_identity:true beside merchant.name:null). They now report what you actually got. Changed in 0.9.0: merchant_identity is no longer equivalent to `merchant.name !== null`. When nothing resolves, merchant.name now carries your own descriptor back (merchant.source = "descriptor") so the transaction still has something to display, and merchant_identity stays false. Branch on merchant_identity or merchant.source, not on the presence of a name.

merchant_identity.description: **True when a merchant was identified**, whether one already in our catalogue or one newly proposed. **Not the same as merchant.name being populated.** When nothing resolves, merchant.name carries your own descriptor back (merchant.source = "descriptor") and this stays false.

transaction_type.description: True when metadata.transaction_type is populated. Distinct from merchant_identity: a bank fee can be typed with no merchant identified.

logos.description: True when merchant.logo_url is populated on this response.

location.description: True when this descriptor yielded a city or country.

subscription_detection.description: True when a catalog row resolved, so its subscription flag was available to consult. Equivalently, metadata.is_subscription is not null.

livemode.description: true when served to a live key; false when served to a test-mode (sk_test_) key. Test-mode responses are enriched the same way but carry no billing or quota impact.

post.summary: Run underwriting analysis on an SMB applicant (JSON)
post.description:
**Two input modes.** `input_mode=enriched` accepts pre-enriched transactions (matching the `/v1/enrich` response shape) and bills underwriting only. `input_mode=raw` runs enrichment per-transaction and bills enrichment + underwriting in one shot.

**For statement files** (CAMT.053 / MT940 / PDF), use the separate multipart endpoint `POST /v1/underwrite/analyze/statement` instead. This JSON endpoint will reject non-JSON bodies with 415.

**Output.** v1 feature bundle: turnover (TTM, 3m, 6m, trend, volatility, optional seasonality), cash position (days negative, overdraft episodes, peak overdraft), customer concentration (top1%, top5%, HHI), recurring revenue/expense streams with detected cadence, debt service, tax payments, statutory contributions.

**Persistence.** Lender-side only. The features payload is retained for 7-day re-fetch (use GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id), then purged. Only billing metadata + the analysis row stay after purge.

**Idempotency.** Two surfaces: (1) the standard `Idempotency-Key` 24h dedup, and (2) a 7-day `(org_id, applicant_id)` window. Re-submitting the same applicant_id returns the original result + `billable=false`. After 7 days, treated as a fresh evaluation event.

**EUR-only in v1.** Multi-currency submissions return 409 `conflict_currency_mix`.

Required scope: `underwriting:write`.

schema.description: Single SMB applicant submission. Accounts may be one or many. Multi-account fixtures sum turnover across accounts and auto-exclude inter-account transfers. EUR-only in v1.

applicant_id.description: Lender's opaque applicant reference. Never used outside the 7-day (org, applicant) idempotency lookup; not persisted as part of transaction content.

input_mode.description: 'raw' runs enrichment per-transaction as part of the analysis; 'enriched' accepts pre-enriched transactions (matching `/v1/enrich` response shape). Both bill exactly one applicant. Enrichment performed inside an analyze call is included in the per-applicant rate, never billed as a second meter.

applicant_type.description: Which regulatory regime this analysis runs under. Defaults to 'business' when omitted, so existing integrations are unaffected. **Never inferred by Distyra**: it selects a regime (GDPR Art 9 special-category suppression, Consumer Credit Directive II duties on you, and EU AI Act Annex III 5(b) obligations from 2 December 2027), not merely a feature set, and an inferred value could not be audited. **A sole trader (eenmanszaak, ZZP, auto-entrepreneur, Einzelunternehmer) is a natural person and must be sent as 'consumer'**, whatever their account is called. 'consumer' requires a separate contractual entitlement and returns a different feature set: see `features`. Sending 'consumer' without that entitlement returns 403.

declared_monthly_income.description: The monthly income the applicant declared to you, in decimal currency units. **Consumer only.** Sending it with `applicant_type: business` returns 400 rather than being ignored, because a supplied figure that silently does nothing is worse than a refusal. Supplying it engages `features.income_corroboration`, which compares your figure against what the statements show and returns a signed `variance_pct` plus an outcome of `corroborated` (within 10%), `partial` (within 25%), `not_corroborated`, or `insufficient_window` (fewer than 3 whole months). The bands are symmetric on purpose: this reports whether the two figures agree, not whether to lend, and an asymmetric band would be us making your credit judgment. The figure is used for nothing else. It does not enter `features.income` and cannot move any other feature.

household.description: **Consumer only.** Sending it with `applicant_type: business` returns 400. Household composition and tenure as you supplied them. Echoed verbatim at `features.affordability.household` and read by nothing: no figure we return depends on it. It is carried so you can apply your own affordability norm against our residual-income and ratio figures in one payload. **Never inferred**: deriving household size from transaction patterns would be unreliable and Article 9 adjacent, since the signals it would key on are childcare, school fees and medical costs. Omit it and `features.affordability.household` is null.

analysis_window.description: Inclusive date window for the analysis. Omit to let the engine auto-detect from the transaction stream (min/max date). A ≥12-month window is required for seasonality_index; shorter windows emit null.

items.description: Per-account opening balance + transaction stream. Inter-account transfers (counterparty_iban matching another account on the submission) are auto-excluded from turnover/recurring/Engine 3.

iban.description: Optional IBAN of the applicant's account. When provided, inter-account transfers (counterparty_iban matching another submitted account's iban) are auto-excluded from turnover, recurring, and Engine 3 outputs.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. v1 is EUR-only. Non-EUR accounts return 409 conflict_currency_mix.

opening_balance.description: Account opening balance at analysis_window.start, in decimal currency units (€). Required for cash-position reconstruction in Engine 1.

committed_limit.description: Committed overdraft / credit-line limit on this account, in decimal currency units (€). Optional. Powers the credit_line_utilization feature (utilization ratio + 30d trend); when no submitted account carries a limit the feature returns null. On the statement path this is extracted from statement headers automatically. Supply it here only for JSON-mode submissions.

items.description: Either an enriched transaction (input_mode=enriched, shape mirrors the `/v1/enrich` response) or a raw transaction (input_mode=raw, just `date`, `amount`, `descriptor_raw`, optional `counterparty_iban`, `id`). Validated per-mode inside the handler; see input_mode for the discriminator. **Enriched mode also accepts `debt_purpose_code`**, an ISO 20022 repayment purpose code (LOAR, HLRP, HLST, CLPR, IHRP, REOD, BKPP, INTE) that you already hold from your own CAMT.053 ingestion. It is what lets a payment to a bank be recognised as a payment on a debt rather than a payment to an organisation that lends money; without it a small regular payment to a curated lender is reported under `counterparty.irregular_credit_payments` instead of `counterparty.debt_service`. Any other purpose code is rejected with 422 rather than ignored. This field is deliberately restricted to the debt codes so that it can never carry a health or social-security purpose code into a consumer report. On the statement path it is extracted from CAMT.053 automatically. **Raw mode also accepts `bank_code_description`** (max 256 chars), the bank's own label for what kind of transaction this is, taken from the ISO 20022 `bank_transaction_code` or its proprietary equivalent: "Incasso", "Geldautomaat", "SEPA Direct Debets CORE SDD". Send it if your bank feed carries it. It is the single highest-confidence classification signal available, because the bank is stating a fact rather than us inferring one from a descriptor string, and it is what distinguishes a direct debit from a card payment from a person-to-person transfer when the descriptor alone is ambiguous. Mirrors the field of the same name on `/v1/enrich`; ignored in enriched mode, where you have already classified the transaction yourself.

features.description: Reserved for hybrid pricing. v1 accepts ['all'] only; per-feature pricing flips on with the AML add-on.

requestBody.description: Single SMB applicant submission. Accounts may be one or many. Multi-account fixtures sum turnover across accounts and auto-exclude inter-account transfers. EUR-only in v1.

200.description: 200 response from POST /v1/underwrite/analyze. The features payload is retained for 7 days for re-fetch on network drop, then purged. The analysis row itself stays for billing audit.

schema.description: 200 response from POST /v1/underwrite/analyze. The features payload is retained for 7 days for re-fetch on network drop, then purged. The analysis row itself stays for billing audit.

id.description: Server-assigned analysis id. Use with GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id to re-fetch within the 7-day retention window.

applicant_id.description: Echoes the request `applicant_id` for client correlation.

applicant_type.description: Echoes the applicant type this analysis ran under, so the response is self-describing for your audit record. 'business' when the request omitted it.

special_category_suppressed_count.description:
**Consumer applicants only.** Absent under `applicant_type: business`, where the layer does not run.

How many transactions had their merchant resolution collapsed because resolving them would have been an inference about health, religion or belief, political opinion, trade-union membership or ethnic origin (GDPR Article 9(1)), or gambling (tracked separately, and not Article 9).

Those transactions are still in the analysis and still count toward every figure: amount, date, direction and cadence are legitimate affordability signals and are retained. What is withheld is the merchant identity, industry, logo, merchant-derived counterparty role and IBAN, and each such transaction is marked `special_category_suppressed: true` in the evidence package.

**Per-category counts are deliberately not provided.** "3 health, 1 religion" about one applicant is itself an Article 9 disclosure at small counts. This single number lets you evidence that the control ran without learning what it caught.

Suppression is not overridable: there is no flag, parameter or header that turns it off for a consumer applicant. See CCD2 Article 18(3), which prohibits special-category data in a creditworthiness assessment outright from 20 November 2026.

analysis_window.description: Resolved window: either the requested window or the auto-detected min/max from the transaction stream.

features.description: Computed feature bundle: `aggregation` (turnover, cash_position, customer_concentration, credit_line_utilization, the last of which is null unless an account declares a committed limit; customer_concentration.inferred_inflows lists inflows that were counted toward the concentration figures despite carrying a role that normally excludes them (supplier, employee, payment_processor, lender, tax_authority, internal_transfer), because that role was guessed rather than established. Each row names the role it would have been excluded as and why the evidence was insufficient. A curated role still excludes and is not listed. The bucket exists because excluding on a guess let an AI-supplied merchant category move top1_pct and hhi; it is empty when there is nothing to report), `recurring` (recurring_revenue, recurring_expense, returned_dd counts), `counterparty` (tax_payments, statutory_contributions, debt_service, supplier_payments, payment-regularity streams over supplier-tagged counterparties; suppliers_tagged=0 means no supplier coverage for this applicant, not "pays nobody"; debt_collection, payments to debt-collection agencies, an adverse signal; collectors_tagged=0 = no collector activity; only collectors whose role is established count toward `payments`, `collectors_tagged` and `total_micros`; one we only infer is listed in `debt_collection.inferred_collections` with its reason instead, so an adverse inference is never reported as established fact, the same treatment `irregular_credit_payments` gives a guessed lender, and note the direction is deliberately opposite to `customer_concentration.inferred_inflows`, where a guess is counted because excluding it would understate risk; irregular_credit_payments, outflows to credit providers that were not counted as debt_service. Three reasons, carried per row: `not_cadenced` (too irregular to establish a schedule), `inferred_provenance` (the only evidence the counterparty is a lender is an AI inference), and `no_debt_evidence` (the counterparty is an established credit provider and the payments are regular, but nothing about the payments says they are payments on a debt, such as the monthly account fee). These amounts remain in debt_capacity.monthly_non_debt_outflows_micros, so they are counted exactly once; the bucket exists so an analyst can see credit-related spending the engine declined to call an obligation. counterparties=0 = nothing uncounted. Correspondingly, each debt_service stream carries `debt_evidence` naming what established it: `purpose_code` (an ISO 20022 repayment code declared by the applicant's own bank), `descriptor_keyword` (a locale repayment term in the raw descriptor) or `material_cadenced_stream` (a cadenced amount above the account-fee floor, the weakest of the three and the one that says only that the payment is too large to be a bank charge)), `debt_capacity` (DSCR + capacity at policy thresholds, with a transparent assumptions block), `anomaly` (null; Engine 4 deferred). **Under `applicant_type: consumer` the bundle also carries `income` and `income_corroboration`, and omits `turnover`, `customer_concentration`, `credit_line_utilization`, `statutory_contributions` and `debt_capacity` rather than nulling them** (a consumer `turnover` of 0 would read as "this applicant earns nothing"). `income` gives per-stream source types (employment / benefits / pension / self_employment / rental / other), a monthly total, a breakdown, stability (amount variation and missed occurrences, because a skipped salary run is invisible to the variation alone), source concentration, and months observed. Two properties of the breakdown are worth relying on: it always sums to `monthly_income_micros`, and a named bucket is only ever credited from an established role. A source type resting on an AI-supplied merchant category still labels its stream, with `source_type_source: inferred`, but its money lands in `unattributed`, so no model can move a figure between the named buckets. Correspondingly a guessed `lender` role cannot drop an inflow from income: it is counted and disclosed in `income.inferred_inflows`, because letting a model lower an applicant's income is the wrongful-decline direction. `income_corroboration` is present only when you supplied `declared_monthly_income`, and is null (not absent) when you did not. `committed_expenditure` groups the recurring outflow streams into categories (housing, utilities, insurance, credit, childcare, alimony, education, tax, other_committed, plus `unattributed`), gives a monthly committed total, an explicit discretionary residual, each credit obligation broken out individually, and the returned-direct-debit count. Two definitions to read before using it. **Committed means recurring, not contractually obliged.** A monthly subscription counts, because deciding which recurring costs an applicant could stop paying is a judgment about their life rather than a fact about their statements; the effect is conservative for residual income and you can rebuild a narrower definition from `categories` and `credit_commitments`. And **discretionary is a residual, never a classification**: nothing is labelled discretionary, so that figure absorbs one-off purchases, cash withdrawals and every outflow too irregular to form a stream. `credit_commitments` is derived from `counterparty.debt_service` rather than recomputed, so the two lists are one fact seen twice and cannot disagree; `uncounted_credit_monthly_micros` tells you when `counterparty.irregular_credit_payments` holds credit-related outflow the engine declined to call an obligation. `affordability` is the consumer analogue of `debt_capacity`: residual income as the headline (income minus committed, in euros rather than a ratio, because 30% of 1,400 and 30% of 6,000 are the same number and not the same situation), plus `debt_to_income_ratio` and `debt_service_to_income_ratio` (credit plus housing). **It publishes no threshold ladder on purpose.** Consumer affordability norms are set per market by regulation and per lender by policy, and inventing one would dress our choice as a standard. `household` is echoed there exactly as you supplied it and is read by nothing; it is never inferred. **Both ratios are a floor whenever `committed_expenditure.categories.unattributed.monthly_micros` is non-zero**, because a commitment whose category rests on an AI-supplied merchant category is not credited to a named bucket. The `assumptions.ratio_basis` string says which case applies on each analysis. Note the total and therefore `residual_income_micros` are unaffected either way. `counterparty.tax_payments` and `counterparty.statutory_contributions` carry established roles only: a public body recognised solely from an AI-supplied category is diverted to `counterparty.inferred_tax_payments` / `counterparty.inferred_statutory_contributions` with its reason, rather than appearing in the primary list with a label. No figure moves when a row diverts, because these buckets feed no capacity calculation; what changes is that a statement of fact to you is no longer made on a guess. Amount fields are stringified micro-EUR bigints so 12-digit values round-trip cleanly through JSON.

engine_versions.description: Per-engine semver. Bump on each engine update so downstream consumers can pin or invalidate cached results.

debt_capacity.description: Derived feature layer (DSCR + capacity). **Null under `applicant_type: consumer`**, where the engine does not run: DSCR presumes a business servicing debt from trading cash flow. Null means "did not run", which is a different statement from a version string. The consumer analogue is a residual-income and debt-to-income layer, not yet shipped.

income.description: Consumer income layer (`features.income`, `features.income_corroboration`). **Null under `applicant_type: business`**, mirroring `debt_capacity` in the other direction: the two are analogues and each is null on the profile where it did not run. The business analogue of income is `turnover`.

committed_expenditure.description: Consumer committed-expenditure layer (`features.committed_expenditure`). Null under `applicant_type: business`.

affordability.description: Consumer affordability layer (`features.affordability`). Null under `applicant_type: business`; it is the analogue of `debt_capacity`, which is null under `consumer`.

anomaly.description: Null in v1. Engine 4 (structuring + transaction anomaly) is deferred to v2.

evidence.description: Transaction-level evidence behind the features: labelled transactions (incl. counterparty_role), balances, the reconciliation trust artifact, parser warnings, and source provenance. Present on /analyze/statement responses only.

reconciled.description: True iff every account balances within tolerance (opening + transactions = closing).

iban_source.description:
Where `iban` came from, so you can weigh it. Null when, and only when, there is no IBAN.

- `received`: **we read it off the statement.** CAMT.053 and CODA always carry one; MT940 usually does; a PDF carries whatever is printed on it, and a misread one is caught by its own ISO 7064 check digits.
- `derived`: **the format carries no IBAN and we reconstructed it** from the domestic account components. Norma 43 (Spain) is the case today: the two dígitos de control the Spanish IBAN needs are a weighted mod-11 of the entidad, oficina and cuenta the file already carries, so the IBAN is a function of fields we read rather than data the file omits.
- `client_asserted`: **you sent it to us.** Every account submitted to `POST /v1/underwrite/analyze/statement/parsed` carries this, because on that route your browser ran the parser and the PDF never reached us, so we did not read the statement and did not compute anything. We do not repeat a provenance claim we cannot check: whatever the submitted body said about this field is discarded and replaced with this value.

**Why this is published rather than kept internal.** A derived IBAN **cannot be checked against anything the bank sent**. Its check digits are computed from the same fields we read, so a field taken at the wrong offset produces a self-consistent IBAN for an account that does not exist, and no validation downstream can see it. A `received` IBAN has the opposite property: somebody else computed its check digits, so they test our reading. `client_asserted` is a third thing again, carrying no claim by us at all. If you reconcile this account number against another system, that difference is the thing to weigh.

residual_micros.description: expected_delta - transaction_sum. "0" on a perfectly balanced statement; non-zero flags a dropped/misparsed transaction.

tolerance_micros.description: Allowed |residual|. "0" for structured formats; calibrated (1 cent/txn, €1 cap) for PDF.

descriptor_raw.description: Null only on a special-category-suppressed transaction (see `special_category_suppressed`), where the raw descriptor is withheld because it is the merchant identity in its least processed form. Always a string otherwise.

merchant_statutory_kind.description: health / pension / accident / sectoral / social_secretariat / social_security / other / null. Set only for statutory bodies (drives the statutory_contributions split); null for everything else, including genuine tax authorities.

counterparty_role.description: The EU-correctness signal. Functional role of the counterparty, or null when untagged. **Business:** tax_authority, lender, customer, supplier, employee, payment_processor, internal_transfer. **Consumer (added 2026-08-12):** employer, benefits_agency, pension_provider, landlord, mortgage_provider, utility, insurer, childcare, alimony_recipient, education. Every value names a payer, never a reason for payment. No role discloses a special category, which is why a suppressed transaction keeps its role. `benefits_agency` and `pension_provider` are deliberately separable from `employer`, and `mortgage_provider` from `lender`, because some lenders may not count benefits toward affordability and housing cost is treated differently from unsecured credit.

special_category_suppressed.description:
**Consumer applicants only.** True when this transaction's merchant resolution was collapsed under GDPR Article 9 / CCD2 Article 18(3). See `special_category_suppressed_count` at the top level.

Read it as "we resolved this and are not telling you", which is a different statement from the null merchant fields on an ordinary unresolved transaction. Amount, date, direction and cadence are intact and the transaction still counts toward every figure; `descriptor_raw`, `descriptor_cleaned`, `merchant_id`, `merchant_industry`, `merchant_subindustry`, the merchant-derived `counterparty_role` and `counterparty_iban` are withheld.

Absent (not false) on every other transaction and on the whole business path.

counterparty_source.description: Provenance of an institutional counterparty_role / merchant_statutory_kind: 'confirmed' (curated catalog row or payer-declared ISO 20022 purpose code) vs 'inferred' (AI category guess). Lets a lender tell a solid obligation from a likely one; inferred rows still count in the totals. Absent on regular merchants.

debt_purpose_code.description: Payer-declared ISO 20022 purpose code, restricted to the debt-repayment codes: LOAR (loan repayment), HLRP / HLST (property loan), CLPR (car loan principal), IHRP (instalment / hire purchase), REOD (overdraft repayment), BKPP (bank loan principal paydown), INTE (interest). Null on every transaction that does not declare one, and on the drawdown codes (LOAN, PLDS, BKDF), the refinancing code (PLRF) and the loan-FEE code (BKFE), none of which is a payment on a debt. This is the strongest of the three signals behind `counterparty.debt_service.debt_evidence`: it comes from the statement rather than from our catalog. Populated automatically from CAMT.053 `<Purp><Cd>`; no other statement format carries a true ISO purpose code.

extraction_method.description:
How the transactions were obtained from this source. **Weigh the output accordingly**: `structured` (CAMT.053, MT940 and the rest) and `deterministic_pdf` / `deterministic_pdf_browser` are rule-based parsers with no model involved. `llm_ocr` is the document-model fallback, used when the deterministic parser cannot read a layout.

Provided so that the person your organisation assigns to oversee this output under AI Act Article 26(2) can tell which of those produced the numbers, which is a different question from whether they balance.

completeness.description:
Whether the extraction was checked against the **control totals the statement declares for itself** (opening + total in − total out = closing).

- `verified`: the statement declared usable totals, they were self-consistent, and they equal what we extracted. The strongest assurance available that no row is missing.
- `unverified_no_control_totals`: the statement declares no usable totals. Common, and not a defect.
- `unverified_totals_inconsistent`: totals were found but failed their own identity, so they describe something other than this transaction list. Discarded rather than trusted.
- `unverified_rows_filtered`: we excluded rows, for example non-EUR transactions or entries that would be counted twice, so a disagreement would prove nothing.
- `unverified_descriptor_integrity`: the extraction's descriptors collapsed to one or two distinct values across a long statement, so merchant resolution and counterparty grouping cannot be trusted even though every figure reconciles. Reported rather than fatal, because low diversity has a legitimate shape (a card used at one shop); an extraction with no descriptors at all is refused outright instead.
- `unverified_descriptor_provenance`: descriptors were returned that do not appear in the text the extractor actually read, so they were produced rather than transcribed off the statement. **This is the only check that can see a descriptor which is present, plausible and wrong.** Every other one is arithmetic, and an invented descriptor changes no total. Reported rather than fatal: measured at 0 ungrounded rows across 630 rows of real statements, so the false-positive rate is bounded but the check is young. Absent only when the extraction route supplies no source text, in which case the question could not be asked and no verdict is claimed either way.
- `unverified_amount_provenance`: amounts were returned that do not appear in the transaction table the extractor read from the page, so at least one figure was not read off the statement. **This is the only check that is not arithmetic**, and therefore the only one that can see two amounts misread in compensating directions: those preserve every total, so both the balance reconciliation and the statement's own declared totals accept them. Absent when the page carries no parseable transaction table.
- `unverified_ocr_fidelity`: descriptors were read consistently by the document model but do not appear in the PDF's own embedded text. **This is the only check sourced from a reading that is not OCR**, and therefore the only one that can see a stable misread: an engine reading the same wrong characters on every run produces a page text and an annotation that agree with each other, so re-running it proves nothing. Divergence is reported only for a near-miss of a real word in a character pair OCR genuinely confuses, which is what keeps rendering differences between the two readings from being reported as defects. Absent when the document carries no usable text layer.
- `unverified_ocr_fidelity` is also set when an account number in a descriptor **fails its own ISO 7064 check digits**. A correctly transcribed IBAN always passes, so a failure means a character was misread. This half of the signal needs no second reading of the page at all, which makes it the one fidelity check that still works on a document with no usable text layer. Mandate references and domestic account ids are excluded by construction: a known country code printed at the wrong length for that country is never treated as an IBAN.
- `unverified_date_integrity` is also set when a transaction's **amount is printed on the page against a different date** than the one reported. The amounts themselves are all present, so every total is preserved and neither balance reconciliation nor the declared control totals can see it. This pairs each amount with the date printed beside it in the statement's own table, so it needs no second extraction.
- `unverified_extraction_reproducibility`: the same document extracted more than once did not return the same transaction set. **This is the only check that does not compare the extraction against the page**, so it is the only one that can see an output which is internally consistent, grounded in the page text and arithmetically sound while simply not being reproducible. It says nothing about which run is correct; the result returned is the most common one. Absent unless repeated extraction is enabled, in which case no claim is made either way.
- `unverified_amount_provenance` is also set when a **declared balance or control total does not appear anywhere on the page it was read from**. Both existing balance checks are internal: one compares the transaction sum to the declared opening-to-closing delta, the other checks the four declared figures against their own identity. A misread balance that stays self-consistent passes them both, and only a comparison against the page can see it.
- `unverified_date_integrity`: transaction dates are not in chronological order, which suggests a row was extracted with the wrong date. **This outranks every value above, including `verified`**, because the others describe whether we could check the extraction while this is evidence the extraction is wrong. A misread date preserves every total, so neither the balance check nor the control totals can see it. It is reported rather than fatal: statements are overwhelmingly chronological (12 of 12 measured), but a bank that groups by transaction type or orders by value date would trip it legitimately.

**Treat anything other than `verified` as "we do not know whether the extraction is complete and faithful."**

Two things this check is for, both measured rather than assumed. **Missing rows:** an extraction is now accepted only if it reconciles against the statement's own declared closing balance, so a missing row is rejected outright rather than surfacing here. The earlier weakness, where a single dropped transaction was silently accepted in most positions on a long statement, was closed on 2026-08-17. **Wrong dates:** reconciliation cannot see an error that preserves the totals, and a transaction placed on the wrong day does exactly that. It was observed twice in 55 real extractions, on two different statements. `unverified_date_integrity` is the only signal that reports it.

billable.description: true when this call consumed quota / triggered a debit. false on 7-day idempotent re-pull (same applicant_id, returns the original result) and on calls within the Starter tier's 50 included applicants.

available_until.description: +7-day re-fetch deadline. After this timestamp the features payload is purged by the retention cron; GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id returns 410 thereafter.
