get.summary: Re-fetch a previous underwriting analysis (7-day window)
get.description:
Returns the original features payload within the 7-day retention window after analyze. Useful when the lender system needs to re-pull after a network drop or page refresh.

**410 Gone** after `features_purged_at` is set (or `features_returned` is null). The analysis row stays for billing audit but the payload cannot be re-fetched. Lenders should persist results their side if they need long-term access.

**404 Not Found** when no row exists for your organization. Scoped to your organization; a uuid belonging to another organization returns 404 (no information leakage).

Required scope: `underwriting:read`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Server-assigned analysis id, as returned by POST /v1/underwrite/analyze.

200.description: 200 response from POST /v1/underwrite/analyze. The features payload is retained for 7 days for re-fetch on network drop, then purged. The analysis row itself stays for billing audit.

schema.description: 200 response from POST /v1/underwrite/analyze. The features payload is retained for 7 days for re-fetch on network drop, then purged. The analysis row itself stays for billing audit.

id.description: Server-assigned analysis id. Use with GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id to re-fetch within the 7-day retention window.

applicant_id.description: Echoes the request `applicant_id` for client correlation.

applicant_type.description: Echoes the applicant type this analysis ran under, so the response is self-describing for your audit record. 'business' when the request omitted it.

special_category_suppressed_count.description:
**Consumer applicants only.** Absent under `applicant_type: business`, where the layer does not run.

How many transactions had their merchant resolution collapsed because resolving them would have been an inference about health, religion or belief, political opinion, trade-union membership or ethnic origin (GDPR Article 9(1)), or gambling (tracked separately, and not Article 9).

Those transactions are still in the analysis and still count toward every figure: amount, date, direction and cadence are legitimate affordability signals and are retained. What is withheld is the merchant identity, industry, logo, merchant-derived counterparty role and IBAN, and each such transaction is marked `special_category_suppressed: true` in the evidence package.

**Per-category counts are deliberately not provided.** "3 health, 1 religion" about one applicant is itself an Article 9 disclosure at small counts. This single number lets you evidence that the control ran without learning what it caught.

Suppression is not overridable: there is no flag, parameter or header that turns it off for a consumer applicant. See CCD2 Article 18(3), which prohibits special-category data in a creditworthiness assessment outright from 20 November 2026.

analysis_window.description: Resolved window: either the requested window or the auto-detected min/max from the transaction stream.

features.description: Computed feature bundle: `aggregation` (turnover, cash_position, customer_concentration, credit_line_utilization, the last of which is null unless an account declares a committed limit; customer_concentration.inferred_inflows lists inflows that were counted toward the concentration figures despite carrying a role that normally excludes them (supplier, employee, payment_processor, lender, tax_authority, internal_transfer), because that role was guessed rather than established. Each row names the role it would have been excluded as and why the evidence was insufficient. A curated role still excludes and is not listed. The bucket exists because excluding on a guess let an AI-supplied merchant category move top1_pct and hhi; it is empty when there is nothing to report), `recurring` (recurring_revenue, recurring_expense, returned_dd counts), `counterparty` (tax_payments, statutory_contributions, debt_service, supplier_payments, payment-regularity streams over supplier-tagged counterparties; suppliers_tagged=0 means no supplier coverage for this applicant, not "pays nobody"; debt_collection, payments to debt-collection agencies, an adverse signal; collectors_tagged=0 = no collector activity; only collectors whose role is established count toward `payments`, `collectors_tagged` and `total_micros`; one we only infer is listed in `debt_collection.inferred_collections` with its reason instead, so an adverse inference is never reported as established fact, the same treatment `irregular_credit_payments` gives a guessed lender, and note the direction is deliberately opposite to `customer_concentration.inferred_inflows`, where a guess is counted because excluding it would understate risk; irregular_credit_payments, outflows to credit providers that were not counted as debt_service. Three reasons, carried per row: `not_cadenced` (too irregular to establish a schedule), `inferred_provenance` (the only evidence the counterparty is a lender is an AI inference), and `no_debt_evidence` (the counterparty is an established credit provider and the payments are regular, but nothing about the payments says they are payments on a debt, such as the monthly account fee). These amounts remain in debt_capacity.monthly_non_debt_outflows_micros, so they are counted exactly once; the bucket exists so an analyst can see credit-related spending the engine declined to call an obligation. counterparties=0 = nothing uncounted. Correspondingly, each debt_service stream carries `debt_evidence` naming what established it: `purpose_code` (an ISO 20022 repayment code declared by the applicant's own bank), `descriptor_keyword` (a locale repayment term in the raw descriptor) or `material_cadenced_stream` (a cadenced amount above the account-fee floor, the weakest of the three and the one that says only that the payment is too large to be a bank charge)), `debt_capacity` (DSCR + capacity at policy thresholds, with a transparent assumptions block), `anomaly` (null; Engine 4 deferred). **Under `applicant_type: consumer` the bundle also carries `income` and `income_corroboration`, and omits `turnover`, `customer_concentration`, `credit_line_utilization`, `statutory_contributions` and `debt_capacity` rather than nulling them** (a consumer `turnover` of 0 would read as "this applicant earns nothing"). `income` gives per-stream source types (employment / benefits / pension / self_employment / rental / other), a monthly total, a breakdown, stability (amount variation and missed occurrences, because a skipped salary run is invisible to the variation alone), source concentration, and months observed. Two properties of the breakdown are worth relying on: it always sums to `monthly_income_micros`, and a named bucket is only ever credited from an established role. A source type resting on an AI-supplied merchant category still labels its stream, with `source_type_source: inferred`, but its money lands in `unattributed`, so no model can move a figure between the named buckets. Correspondingly a guessed `lender` role cannot drop an inflow from income: it is counted and disclosed in `income.inferred_inflows`, because letting a model lower an applicant's income is the wrongful-decline direction. `income_corroboration` is present only when you supplied `declared_monthly_income`, and is null (not absent) when you did not. `committed_expenditure` groups the recurring outflow streams into categories (housing, utilities, insurance, credit, childcare, alimony, education, tax, other_committed, plus `unattributed`), gives a monthly committed total, an explicit discretionary residual, each credit obligation broken out individually, and the returned-direct-debit count. Two definitions to read before using it. **Committed means recurring, not contractually obliged.** A monthly subscription counts, because deciding which recurring costs an applicant could stop paying is a judgment about their life rather than a fact about their statements; the effect is conservative for residual income and you can rebuild a narrower definition from `categories` and `credit_commitments`. And **discretionary is a residual, never a classification**: nothing is labelled discretionary, so that figure absorbs one-off purchases, cash withdrawals and every outflow too irregular to form a stream. `credit_commitments` is derived from `counterparty.debt_service` rather than recomputed, so the two lists are one fact seen twice and cannot disagree; `uncounted_credit_monthly_micros` tells you when `counterparty.irregular_credit_payments` holds credit-related outflow the engine declined to call an obligation. `affordability` is the consumer analogue of `debt_capacity`: residual income as the headline (income minus committed, in euros rather than a ratio, because 30% of 1,400 and 30% of 6,000 are the same number and not the same situation), plus `debt_to_income_ratio` and `debt_service_to_income_ratio` (credit plus housing). **It publishes no threshold ladder on purpose.** Consumer affordability norms are set per market by regulation and per lender by policy, and inventing one would dress our choice as a standard. `household` is echoed there exactly as you supplied it and is read by nothing; it is never inferred. **Both ratios are a floor whenever `committed_expenditure.categories.unattributed.monthly_micros` is non-zero**, because a commitment whose category rests on an AI-supplied merchant category is not credited to a named bucket. The `assumptions.ratio_basis` string says which case applies on each analysis. Note the total and therefore `residual_income_micros` are unaffected either way. `counterparty.tax_payments` and `counterparty.statutory_contributions` carry established roles only: a public body recognised solely from an AI-supplied category is diverted to `counterparty.inferred_tax_payments` / `counterparty.inferred_statutory_contributions` with its reason, rather than appearing in the primary list with a label. No figure moves when a row diverts, because these buckets feed no capacity calculation; what changes is that a statement of fact to you is no longer made on a guess. Amount fields are stringified micro-EUR bigints so 12-digit values round-trip cleanly through JSON.

engine_versions.description: Per-engine semver. Bump on each engine update so downstream consumers can pin or invalidate cached results.

debt_capacity.description: Derived feature layer (DSCR + capacity). **Null under `applicant_type: consumer`**, where the engine does not run: DSCR presumes a business servicing debt from trading cash flow. Null means "did not run", which is a different statement from a version string. The consumer analogue is a residual-income and debt-to-income layer, not yet shipped.

income.description: Consumer income layer (`features.income`, `features.income_corroboration`). **Null under `applicant_type: business`**, mirroring `debt_capacity` in the other direction: the two are analogues and each is null on the profile where it did not run. The business analogue of income is `turnover`.

committed_expenditure.description: Consumer committed-expenditure layer (`features.committed_expenditure`). Null under `applicant_type: business`.

affordability.description: Consumer affordability layer (`features.affordability`). Null under `applicant_type: business`; it is the analogue of `debt_capacity`, which is null under `consumer`.

anomaly.description: Null in v1. Engine 4 (structuring + transaction anomaly) is deferred to v2.

evidence.description: Transaction-level evidence behind the features: labelled transactions (incl. counterparty_role), balances, the reconciliation trust artifact, parser warnings, and source provenance. Present on /analyze/statement responses only.

reconciled.description: True iff every account balances within tolerance (opening + transactions = closing).

iban_source.description:
Where `iban` came from, so you can weigh it. Null when, and only when, there is no IBAN.

- `received`: **we read it off the statement.** CAMT.053 and CODA always carry one; MT940 usually does; a PDF carries whatever is printed on it, and a misread one is caught by its own ISO 7064 check digits.
- `derived`: **the format carries no IBAN and we reconstructed it** from the domestic account components. Norma 43 (Spain) is the case today: the two dígitos de control the Spanish IBAN needs are a weighted mod-11 of the entidad, oficina and cuenta the file already carries, so the IBAN is a function of fields we read rather than data the file omits.
- `client_asserted`: **you sent it to us.** Every account submitted to `POST /v1/underwrite/analyze/statement/parsed` carries this, because on that route your browser ran the parser and the PDF never reached us, so we did not read the statement and did not compute anything. We do not repeat a provenance claim we cannot check: whatever the submitted body said about this field is discarded and replaced with this value.

**Why this is published rather than kept internal.** A derived IBAN **cannot be checked against anything the bank sent**. Its check digits are computed from the same fields we read, so a field taken at the wrong offset produces a self-consistent IBAN for an account that does not exist, and no validation downstream can see it. A `received` IBAN has the opposite property: somebody else computed its check digits, so they test our reading. `client_asserted` is a third thing again, carrying no claim by us at all. If you reconcile this account number against another system, that difference is the thing to weigh.

residual_micros.description: expected_delta - transaction_sum. "0" on a perfectly balanced statement; non-zero flags a dropped/misparsed transaction.

tolerance_micros.description: Allowed |residual|. "0" for structured formats; calibrated (1 cent/txn, €1 cap) for PDF.

descriptor_raw.description: Null only on a special-category-suppressed transaction (see `special_category_suppressed`), where the raw descriptor is withheld because it is the merchant identity in its least processed form. Always a string otherwise.

merchant_statutory_kind.description: health / pension / accident / sectoral / social_secretariat / social_security / other / null. Set only for statutory bodies (drives the statutory_contributions split); null for everything else, including genuine tax authorities.

counterparty_role.description: The EU-correctness signal. Functional role of the counterparty, or null when untagged. **Business:** tax_authority, lender, customer, supplier, employee, payment_processor, internal_transfer. **Consumer (added 2026-08-12):** employer, benefits_agency, pension_provider, landlord, mortgage_provider, utility, insurer, childcare, alimony_recipient, education. Every value names a payer, never a reason for payment. No role discloses a special category, which is why a suppressed transaction keeps its role. `benefits_agency` and `pension_provider` are deliberately separable from `employer`, and `mortgage_provider` from `lender`, because some lenders may not count benefits toward affordability and housing cost is treated differently from unsecured credit.

special_category_suppressed.description:
**Consumer applicants only.** True when this transaction's merchant resolution was collapsed under GDPR Article 9 / CCD2 Article 18(3). See `special_category_suppressed_count` at the top level.

Read it as "we resolved this and are not telling you", which is a different statement from the null merchant fields on an ordinary unresolved transaction. Amount, date, direction and cadence are intact and the transaction still counts toward every figure; `descriptor_raw`, `descriptor_cleaned`, `merchant_id`, `merchant_industry`, `merchant_subindustry`, the merchant-derived `counterparty_role` and `counterparty_iban` are withheld.

Absent (not false) on every other transaction and on the whole business path.

counterparty_source.description: Provenance of an institutional counterparty_role / merchant_statutory_kind: 'confirmed' (curated catalog row or payer-declared ISO 20022 purpose code) vs 'inferred' (AI category guess). Lets a lender tell a solid obligation from a likely one; inferred rows still count in the totals. Absent on regular merchants.

debt_purpose_code.description: Payer-declared ISO 20022 purpose code, restricted to the debt-repayment codes: LOAR (loan repayment), HLRP / HLST (property loan), CLPR (car loan principal), IHRP (instalment / hire purchase), REOD (overdraft repayment), BKPP (bank loan principal paydown), INTE (interest). Null on every transaction that does not declare one, and on the drawdown codes (LOAN, PLDS, BKDF), the refinancing code (PLRF) and the loan-FEE code (BKFE), none of which is a payment on a debt. This is the strongest of the three signals behind `counterparty.debt_service.debt_evidence`: it comes from the statement rather than from our catalog. Populated automatically from CAMT.053 `<Purp><Cd>`; no other statement format carries a true ISO purpose code.

extraction_method.description:
How the transactions were obtained from this source. **Weigh the output accordingly**: `structured` (CAMT.053, MT940 and the rest) and `deterministic_pdf` / `deterministic_pdf_browser` are rule-based parsers with no model involved. `llm_ocr` is the document-model fallback, used when the deterministic parser cannot read a layout.

Provided so that the person your organisation assigns to oversee this output under AI Act Article 26(2) can tell which of those produced the numbers, which is a different question from whether they balance.

completeness.description:
Whether the extraction was checked against the **control totals the statement declares for itself** (opening + total in − total out = closing).

- `verified`: the statement declared usable totals, they were self-consistent, and they equal what we extracted. The strongest assurance available that no row is missing.
- `unverified_no_control_totals`: the statement declares no usable totals. Common, and not a defect.
- `unverified_totals_inconsistent`: totals were found but failed their own identity, so they describe something other than this transaction list. Discarded rather than trusted.
- `unverified_rows_filtered`: we excluded rows, for example non-EUR transactions or entries that would be counted twice, so a disagreement would prove nothing.
- `unverified_descriptor_integrity`: the extraction's descriptors collapsed to one or two distinct values across a long statement, so merchant resolution and counterparty grouping cannot be trusted even though every figure reconciles. Reported rather than fatal, because low diversity has a legitimate shape (a card used at one shop); an extraction with no descriptors at all is refused outright instead.
- `unverified_descriptor_provenance`: descriptors were returned that do not appear in the text the extractor actually read, so they were produced rather than transcribed off the statement. **This is the only check that can see a descriptor which is present, plausible and wrong.** Every other one is arithmetic, and an invented descriptor changes no total. Reported rather than fatal: measured at 0 ungrounded rows across 630 rows of real statements, so the false-positive rate is bounded but the check is young. Absent only when the extraction route supplies no source text, in which case the question could not be asked and no verdict is claimed either way.
- `unverified_amount_provenance`: amounts were returned that do not appear in the transaction table the extractor read from the page, so at least one figure was not read off the statement. **This is the only check that is not arithmetic**, and therefore the only one that can see two amounts misread in compensating directions: those preserve every total, so both the balance reconciliation and the statement's own declared totals accept them. Absent when the page carries no parseable transaction table.
- `unverified_ocr_fidelity`: descriptors were read consistently by the document model but do not appear in the PDF's own embedded text. **This is the only check sourced from a reading that is not OCR**, and therefore the only one that can see a stable misread: an engine reading the same wrong characters on every run produces a page text and an annotation that agree with each other, so re-running it proves nothing. Divergence is reported only for a near-miss of a real word in a character pair OCR genuinely confuses, which is what keeps rendering differences between the two readings from being reported as defects. Absent when the document carries no usable text layer.
- `unverified_ocr_fidelity` is also set when an account number in a descriptor **fails its own ISO 7064 check digits**. A correctly transcribed IBAN always passes, so a failure means a character was misread. This half of the signal needs no second reading of the page at all, which makes it the one fidelity check that still works on a document with no usable text layer. Mandate references and domestic account ids are excluded by construction: a known country code printed at the wrong length for that country is never treated as an IBAN.
- `unverified_date_integrity` is also set when a transaction's **amount is printed on the page against a different date** than the one reported. The amounts themselves are all present, so every total is preserved and neither balance reconciliation nor the declared control totals can see it. This pairs each amount with the date printed beside it in the statement's own table, so it needs no second extraction.
- `unverified_extraction_reproducibility`: the same document extracted more than once did not return the same transaction set. **This is the only check that does not compare the extraction against the page**, so it is the only one that can see an output which is internally consistent, grounded in the page text and arithmetically sound while simply not being reproducible. It says nothing about which run is correct; the result returned is the most common one. Absent unless repeated extraction is enabled, in which case no claim is made either way.
- `unverified_amount_provenance` is also set when a **declared balance or control total does not appear anywhere on the page it was read from**. Both existing balance checks are internal: one compares the transaction sum to the declared opening-to-closing delta, the other checks the four declared figures against their own identity. A misread balance that stays self-consistent passes them both, and only a comparison against the page can see it.
- `unverified_date_integrity`: transaction dates are not in chronological order, which suggests a row was extracted with the wrong date. **This outranks every value above, including `verified`**, because the others describe whether we could check the extraction while this is evidence the extraction is wrong. A misread date preserves every total, so neither the balance check nor the control totals can see it. It is reported rather than fatal: statements are overwhelmingly chronological (12 of 12 measured), but a bank that groups by transaction type or orders by value date would trip it legitimately.

**Treat anything other than `verified` as "we do not know whether the extraction is complete and faithful."**

Two things this check is for, both measured rather than assumed. **Missing rows:** an extraction is now accepted only if it reconciles against the statement's own declared closing balance, so a missing row is rejected outright rather than surfacing here. The earlier weakness, where a single dropped transaction was silently accepted in most positions on a long statement, was closed on 2026-08-17. **Wrong dates:** reconciliation cannot see an error that preserves the totals, and a transaction placed on the wrong day does exactly that. It was observed twice in 55 real extractions, on two different statements. `unverified_date_integrity` is the only signal that reports it.

get.summary: Download a statement evidence report (PDF or CSV)
get.description:
Returns the statement evidence behind an analysis as a downloadable document: a branded **PDF** (reconciliation, balances, and the labelled transaction table incl. counterparty roles) or a **CSV** of the labelled transactions for spreadsheet use.

**`?format=pdf` (default) | `csv`.**

Available only for statement-mode analyses (`POST /v1/underwrite/analyze/statement`) within the 7-day retention window. **404** for JSON-mode analyses (no statement evidence) or unknown ids; **410** once the evidence payload has been purged.

Required scope: `underwriting:read`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Output format. `pdf` (default) for the branded report, `csv` for the transaction rows.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Server-assigned analysis id, as returned by POST /v1/underwrite/analyze.

get.summary: List past underwriting analyses (billing transparency)
get.description:
Paginated list of analyses for the calling organization, ordered by `created_at DESC, id DESC`. Returns metadata only. Features payloads are accessed via GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id within the 7-day window.

**Pagination.** Cursor-based: pass back `next_cursor` from the previous response in the `cursor` query parameter. `next_cursor` is null on the last page. Cursors are stable across rows that share a `created_at` (id breaks ties).

**Filtering.** Optional `applicant_id` exact-match filter. Combine with `limit` for typical "show me this applicant's analysis history" queries.

**Use cases.** Billing transparency, applicant history, post-purge audit (rows show `features_purged: true` once the 7-day window elapses).

Required scope: `underwriting:read`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum items to return on this page. Server may return fewer if there is no more data.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned in `next_cursor` of the previous response. Format: `<iso-timestamp>|<uuid>` (clients should treat it as opaque).

parameters.name: applicant_id
parameters.description: Filter to a single applicant_id. Exact-match only.

200.description: Page of past analyses for billing transparency. Scoped to your organization; only your organization's rows are visible.

schema.description: Page of past analyses for billing transparency. Scoped to your organization; only your organization's rows are visible.

items.description: Metadata-only row. The features payload is deliberately left out. Re-fetch via GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id within the 7-day window.

applicant_ref.description: The lender's own reference for Distyra Connect analyses, joined from the originating connection. For connect-originated analyses `applicant_id` is the connection id (the data-source identity used for idempotency), and this is the human reference the lender set on the connection. null for direct JSON /analyze submissions, where the lender's reference is already `applicant_id`.

billable.description: false for 7-day idempotent re-pulls and for calls within the included-quota tier.

billed_amount_micros.description: Stringified bigint (micro-EUR). The per-applicant underwriting charge for this analyze call (enrichment performed inside the call is included in the per-applicant rate, never a second component).

features_purged.description: true if the features payload has been wiped by the 7-day retention purge. GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id returns 410 for these.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Null when there are no more rows. Pass back via the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page.

post.summary: Upload a bank statement (or ZIP of statements) and return parsed transactions
post.description:
Multipart upload of a single bank statement file (CAMT.053 XML, SWIFT MT940 text, CFONB 120 fixed-width (the French SME default for BNP Paribas, Société Générale and Crédit Agricole), or PDF), or a ZIP archive containing multiple such files (typical Sparkasse / German Anlage-3 fan-out shape: one CAMT.053 per account per day). Returns the parsed account shape immediately plus a 7-day re-fetch handle.

**When to use this vs `/v1/underwrite/analyze/statement`:** use this `/ingest` endpoint when you want the parsed shape back to inspect, store, or transform before deciding to analyze (or when you want to bill the parse cost separately from analyze). Use `/v1/underwrite/analyze/statement` when you want to upload statement files and run the analyze engines in a single bundled call. That path charges one combined ledger entry covering analyze + N×ingest.

**Single file vs ZIP: polymorphic response.** When the upload is a single statement file, the response is the single-file shape with `bundle_id: null`. When the upload is a ZIP, the response is the bundle envelope (`bundle_id` + per-file `ingestions[]`). Discriminate via presence of `ingestions[]`. For an explicit multi-file endpoint that always returns the bundle envelope, see `POST /v1/underwrite/ingest/batch`.

**Format detection.** Default is `auto`, which sniffs magic bytes from the first 1KB. Pass `?format=camt053|mt940|cfonb120|coda|norma43|cbi|bgmax|pdf` to skip sniffing. The format query parameter applies to every entry in a ZIP. Mixed-format ZIPs are supported only via `auto`.

**Retention.** Default is 7 days for both the parsed shape (re-fetched via GET /v1/underwrite/ingestions/:id) and the raw uploaded bytes (stored in OVH Object Storage, GRA region). Pass `?retain_for_debug=false` to force immediate purge of the raw file. The parsed shape still persists for 7d billing audit. Organizations may set their default to `zero` via the admin UI to lock this down regardless of the per-call flag. For ZIP uploads the retention policy applies per-extracted-entry; the ZIP container itself is not retained separately.

**Limits.** 25MB max per file. ZIP archives subject to 25MB compressed, ~500MB uncompressed total, 500 entries.

**Billing.** One billable event per file. Per-format rates from the subscription (defaults: €0.05 CAMT.053, €0.05 MT940, €0.05 CFONB 120, €1.00 PDF). For ZIP uploads, files are processed serially; if a charge fails mid-batch the response returns 402 with `incomplete: true` and the bundle envelope listing the files that did land. Customer pays only for what landed.

**Enrichment (`?enrich=true`).** By default the parsed transactions carry the raw parser shape (date, amount, raw descriptor). Pass `?enrich=true` to also enrich every parsed transaction (paid), the same enrichment as `/v1/enrich` and `/v1/underwrite/analyze/statement?enrich=true`, returning `descriptor_cleaned`, `merchant_id`, `merchant_industry`, `transaction_type`, and `counterparty_role` per transaction. Enrichment bills per transaction at the enrichment rate as a separate ledger entry (reported in `enrichment_billed_micros`), on top of the per-file ingest charge. The enriched shape also persists for the 7d re-fetch window. For ZIP uploads, enrichment applies per file with the same pay-only-for-what-landed semantics.

**Sales-led.** Standalone statement ingestion is enabled per organization after a conversation with us ([contact us](https://www.distyra.eu/contact)); until then this endpoint returns 402 `sales_led_only`. To analyse statements for a lending decision instead, use `POST /v1/underwrite/analyze/statement`: it is not subject to this enablement, but it runs a full underwriting analysis, bills per applicant and needs an Underwriting subscription.

Required scope: `underwriting:write`.

file.description: One statement file (CAMT.053 XML, MT940, CFONB 120, CODA, Norma 43, CBI, BGMAX or PDF), or a ZIP containing several. The part name is not enforced: the first file part wins.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Statement format. `auto` (default) sniffs the magic bytes: `<?xml` → camt053 (or cbi if a `<CBIBdy*>` envelope is present), `:20:` or `{1:` → mt940, opening `01` record code → cfonb120, opening `00000` header → coda (Belgian Febelfin), opening `11` record code → norma43 (Spanish AEB Cuaderno 43), opening `01BGMAX` header → bgmax (Swedish Bankgirot receivables; SEK + EUR), `%PDF` → pdf. `cbi` currently supports the XML envelope variant only; the legacy 120-char tracciato is rejected with a deferred-spec error. `bgmax` is receivables-only (no opening balance, no debits); cash-position features degrade gracefully for BGMAX-only uploads.

parameters.name: enrich
parameters.description: When true, runs paid enrichment on every parsed transaction (matches `/v1/enrich` quality). Additional per-transaction enrichment fee applies, reported in `enrichment_billed_micros`. Default false.

parameters.name: applicant_type
parameters.description: Only meaningful with `?enrich=true`. Set `consumer` when the statement belongs to a natural person: enrichment then runs the GDPR Article 9 / CCD2 Article 18(3) suppression layer, so merchant resolutions that would be an inference about health, religion or belief, political opinion, trade-union membership or ethnic origin are collapsed before they reach the response or the 7-day re-fetch. Requires the consumer underwriting contract (403 `consumer_underwriting_not_entitled` without it). Defaults to `business`.

format.description: Statement format. `auto` (default) sniffs the magic bytes: `<?xml` → camt053 (or cbi if a `<CBIBdy*>` envelope is present), `:20:` or `{1:` → mt940, opening `01` record code → cfonb120, opening `00000` header → coda (Belgian Febelfin), opening `11` record code → norma43 (Spanish AEB Cuaderno 43), opening `01BGMAX` header → bgmax (Swedish Bankgirot receivables; SEK + EUR), `%PDF` → pdf. `cbi` currently supports the XML envelope variant only; the legacy 120-char tracciato is rejected with a deferred-spec error. `bgmax` is receivables-only (no opening balance, no debits); cash-position features degrade gracefully for BGMAX-only uploads.

raw_file_retained.description: true when the raw uploaded bytes were stored in OVH Object Storage (7d lifecycle). false when retain_for_debug=false or the org default is zero-retention.

bundle_id.description: Non-null when this ingestion was part of a multi-file bundle (ZIP upload, or multi-file multipart via POST /v1/underwrite/ingest/batch). Null on single-file calls.

enriched.description: true when `?enrich=true` enriched the transactions (paid). The transactions in `accounts[]` then carry the enriched shape (`descriptor_cleaned`, `merchant_id`, `merchant_industry`, `transaction_type`, `counterparty_role`) instead of the raw parser shape, and GET /v1/underwrite/ingestions/:id re-serves the enriched shape within the 7d window.

enrichment_billed_micros.description: bigint serialized as string. Enrichment debit for this call (separate ledger entry, billed per transaction at the enrichment rate, the same as `/v1/enrich`). "0" when `?enrich` was not set, when covered by the enrichment plan's included quota, or for test-mode keys.

file_count.description: Total usable files in the bundle (excluding ZIP entries skipped via the allowlist).

processed_count.description: How many files were fully ingested. Equals file_count on success; lower when the batch stopped early (typically insufficient credit mid-batch; see `incomplete_reason`).

incomplete.description: true when processed_count < file_count. Customer paid only for what landed; remaining files can be retried after the underlying issue is resolved.

filename.description: Filename as it appeared in the ZIP archive or multipart part. Null when no filename was provided.

billed_amount_micros.description: bigint serialized as string. The per-file ingest charge only. The enrichment debit (when `?enrich=true`) is reported separately in `enrichment_billed_micros`.

skipped.description: ZIP entries excluded by the statement-format allowlist (directories, dotfiles, .csv, etc.). Empty array on multipart uploads.

post.summary: Multi-file statement upload (multipart-with-N-files or ZIP)
post.description:
Explicit multi-file ingest. Accepts either a single ZIP file part (server-side unpack) or multiple file parts in one multipart body (each part is one statement file). Always returns the bundle envelope: `{ bundle_id, source, file_count, processed_count, ingestions[], skipped[], available_until }`.

**When to use this vs `POST /v1/underwrite/ingest`:** use `/ingest/batch` when you always want the bundle envelope, regardless of file count (cleaner client code than discriminating on `bundle_id` presence). Use `/ingest` when you want the polymorphic shape (single file → single response, ZIP → bundle).

**Limits.** 25MB per file. 100MB total compressed (multi-file path) or ~500MB uncompressed total (ZIP path). 500 files / entries.

**Billing.** One ledger entry per file. Per-format rates from the subscription (same as `/ingest`). If a charge fails mid-batch, the response returns 402 with `incomplete: true` and the partial bundle. Customer pays only for what landed.

**Enrichment (`?enrich=true`).** Same semantics as `POST /v1/underwrite/ingest`: enriches the transactions in each file, billed per transaction as a separate ledger entry, reported per file in `ingestions[].enrichment_billed_micros`.

**Strategy gate.** Same sales-led gate as `POST /v1/underwrite/ingest`. Returns 402 `sales_led_only` unless `organizations.statement_ingest_contract` is true. `POST /v1/underwrite/analyze/statement` is unaffected.

Required scope: `underwriting:write`.

files.description: Two or more statement files. Part names are not enforced; every file part is read.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Statement format. `auto` (default) sniffs the magic bytes: `<?xml` → camt053 (or cbi if a `<CBIBdy*>` envelope is present), `:20:` or `{1:` → mt940, opening `01` record code → cfonb120, opening `00000` header → coda (Belgian Febelfin), opening `11` record code → norma43 (Spanish AEB Cuaderno 43), opening `01BGMAX` header → bgmax (Swedish Bankgirot receivables; SEK + EUR), `%PDF` → pdf. `cbi` currently supports the XML envelope variant only; the legacy 120-char tracciato is rejected with a deferred-spec error. `bgmax` is receivables-only (no opening balance, no debits); cash-position features degrade gracefully for BGMAX-only uploads.

parameters.name: enrich
parameters.description: When true, runs paid enrichment on every parsed transaction in every file (matches `/v1/enrich` quality). Additional per-transaction enrichment fee applies, reported per file in `ingestions[].enrichment_billed_micros`. Default false.

parameters.name: applicant_type
parameters.description: Only meaningful with `?enrich=true`. Set `consumer` when the statement belongs to a natural person: enrichment then runs the GDPR Article 9 / CCD2 Article 18(3) suppression layer, so merchant resolutions that would be an inference about health, religion or belief, political opinion, trade-union membership or ethnic origin are collapsed before they reach the response or the 7-day re-fetch. Requires the consumer underwriting contract (403 `consumer_underwriting_not_entitled` without it). Defaults to `business`.

file_count.description: Total usable files in the bundle (excluding ZIP entries skipped via the allowlist).

processed_count.description: How many files were fully ingested. Equals file_count on success; lower when the batch stopped early (typically insufficient credit mid-batch; see `incomplete_reason`).

incomplete.description: true when processed_count < file_count. Customer paid only for what landed; remaining files can be retried after the underlying issue is resolved.

filename.description: Filename as it appeared in the ZIP archive or multipart part. Null when no filename was provided.

format.description: Statement format. `auto` (default) sniffs the magic bytes: `<?xml` → camt053 (or cbi if a `<CBIBdy*>` envelope is present), `:20:` or `{1:` → mt940, opening `01` record code → cfonb120, opening `00000` header → coda (Belgian Febelfin), opening `11` record code → norma43 (Spanish AEB Cuaderno 43), opening `01BGMAX` header → bgmax (Swedish Bankgirot receivables; SEK + EUR), `%PDF` → pdf. `cbi` currently supports the XML envelope variant only; the legacy 120-char tracciato is rejected with a deferred-spec error. `bgmax` is receivables-only (no opening balance, no debits); cash-position features degrade gracefully for BGMAX-only uploads.

billed_amount_micros.description: bigint serialized as string. The per-file ingest charge only. The enrichment debit (when `?enrich=true`) is reported separately in `enrichment_billed_micros`.

skipped.description: ZIP entries excluded by the statement-format allowlist (directories, dotfiles, .csv, etc.). Empty array on multipart uploads.

get.summary: Re-fetch a previous ingestion within the 7d window
get.description:
Returns the parsed account shape from an earlier upload. 410 Gone once `account_purged_at` is set (7 days post-ingest); the row itself remains for billing audit. If the original ingest ran with `?enrich=true`, the persisted transactions carry the enriched shape (`descriptor_cleaned`, `merchant_id`, `transaction_type`, ...). This endpoint re-serves exactly what the POST returned.

Required scope: `underwriting:read`.

get.summary: List past ingestions (billing transparency)
get.description:
Paginated list of ingestions for the calling organization, ordered by `created_at DESC, id DESC`. Returns metadata only. Re-fetch the parsed shape via GET /v1/underwrite/ingestions/:id within the 7d window.

**Pagination.** Cursor-based: pass back `next_cursor` from the previous response in the `cursor` query parameter. `next_cursor` is null on the last page.

**Filtering.** Optional `format` exact-match filter.

Required scope: `underwriting:read`.

post.summary: Mint a borrower statement-collection link
post.description:
Creates a single-use, expiring, lender-scoped link and returns its borrower URL once. Send the URL to the borrower; they open a Distyra-hosted page, consent, and upload bank statements that auto-analyze under your organization. You are notified on completion via the `analysis.completed` webhook and can re-fetch the result with GET /v1/underwrite/analyses/:id.

**Required scope:** `underwriting:write`.

application_ref.description: Your reference for this borrower/application. Becomes the applicant_id on the resulting analysis so you can correlate the result.

expires_in_days.description: How long the link stays openable before it auto-expires. Default 7.

url.description: The Distyra-hosted borrower URL, shown once. Send it to the borrower; it cannot be recovered (only its hash is stored). The borrower opens it, consents, and uploads statements that ingest under your org.

get.summary: List your collection links
get.description:
Your collection links, newest first, cursor-paginated. Pass back `next_cursor` in the `cursor` query param for the next page (null on the last page). The borrower URL is not included. It is shown only on create.

**Required scope:** `underwriting:read`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max links to return (1-100, default 50).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from `next_cursor` of the previous response. Format `<iso-timestamp>|<uuid>`; treat as opaque.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; null on the last page. Pass back via `cursor`.

post.summary: Stage a statement file on a collection link
post.description:
Uploads one statement file to the link's staging area (encrypted at rest, EU). Files accumulate until `finish-analyze` runs one consolidated analysis over the whole bundle and deletes the staged copies. Abandoned staged files are automatically purged by a 7-day storage lifecycle. Multipart: a single file part. Requires the link to be active (consented) and unexpired.

Required scope: `underwriting:write`.

file.description: One statement file to add to this link staging area. The part name is not enforced: the first file part wins. Call once per file; finish-analyze then runs a single consolidated analysis over the whole bundle.

post.summary: Run one consolidated analysis over the staged files and complete the link
post.description:
Loads every staged file, submits one background analysis over the whole bundle (same-IBAN fragments consolidate across files; the merged window feeds the engines; gaps surface as `balance_chain_break` evidence warnings), deletes the staged copies, and flips the link to completed. `applicant_id` is the link's application_ref. Returns 202 + the analysis job id; subscribe to `analysis.completed` or poll the async status endpoint.

Required scope: `underwriting:write`.

post.summary: Submit a large batch for background enrichment
post.description:
Accepts up to 10000 items and returns 202 with a job id. Track progress via GET /v1/enrich/batch/async/{id} or subscribe to the `batch.completed` / `batch.failed` webhook events. Per-item failures surface inside the result array on completion; one bad row never fails the whole batch. Pre-debited at submission time at the same rate as the synchronous /v1/enrich/batch endpoint.

**Our AI provider.** To identify a merchant, or to check that a merchant we identified matches the transaction, we may send the transaction to our AI provider, an EU sub-processor under a zero-retention, no-training agreement, together with its amount, currency, MCC and country. This endpoint has no `cache_only`; to prevent it, use POST /v1/enrich/batch with `cache_only=true`.

**Retention.** The transactions you submit are discarded as soon as the batch reaches a terminal state, since they are needed only while it runs. The result stays fetchable until `expires_at`, 24 hours after submission, after which the row flips to `expired` and the result is gone too. Fetch results you need to keep, or subscribe to `batch.completed` and store them your side.

**Required scope:** `enrichment:write`.

get.summary: Get status + result of a submitted async batch
get.description:
Returns the current state of a previously-submitted async batch. While `pending`/`running`, `result` is null. On `completed`, `result` holds the same shape as POST /v1/enrich/batch (one entry per submitted item, in the same order). On `failed`, `error` carries the terminal reason.

**Retention.** The transactions you submitted are discarded as soon as the batch reaches a terminal state, since they are needed only while it runs. The `result` stays fetchable until `expires_at`, 24 hours after submission, after which the row flips to `expired` and the result is gone too. Fetch results you need to keep, or subscribe to `batch.completed` and store them your side.

**Required scope:** `enrichment:read`.

post.summary: Submit a correction for a previously-enriched transaction
post.description:
Records the customer's correction against the (descriptor, merchant) tuple. Goes into your feedback queue; corrections are reviewed before being promoted into the shared catalog. Re-submitting the same correction is idempotent at the count-of-signals level; duplicates are not deduplicated, by design (each occurrence is a fresh confidence signal).

**Required scope:** `feedback:write`.

schema.description: At least one of `corrected_merchant_id` or `corrected_merchant_name` must be provided.

descriptor.description: The original transaction descriptor as passed to /v1/enrich.

corrected_merchant_id.description: Catalog id of the merchant that should have been returned. Use this when the right merchant exists in the catalog (lookup via /v1/merchants/{id} or by trial enrichment).

corrected_merchant_name.description: Free-text name of the right merchant when no catalog id is known. It goes to our review queue, and the merchant may then be added to our catalogue.

note.description: Optional free-text context (e.g. "this is a French chain not the German one").

requestBody.description: At least one of `corrected_merchant_id` or `corrected_merchant_name` must be provided.

id.description: Server-generated id of the persisted feedback row.

descriptor_hash.description: The hash of the descriptor this feedback is keyed on. The same descriptor sent to /v1/enrich produces the same hash.

post.summary: Register a webhook endpoint
post.description:
Creates a webhook endpoint and returns the raw signing secret once. The secret is HMAC-SHA256-applied to every outbound delivery; verify with the `X-Distyra-Signature` header per the docs. Lost secrets must be rotated.

The endpoint takes the mode of the key: one created with a test key receives only events about test-mode activity (a sandbox connection going active, say), and one created with a live key only live events. Your plan's endpoint limit applies to each mode separately.

**Required scope:** `webhooks:write`.

url.description: HTTPS URL to receive events. Plain HTTP rejected.

events.description: Subset of supported events to subscribe to. Defaults to all currently-supported.

livemode.description: false for an endpoint created with a test key. It receives events about test-mode activity only, and a live endpoint only live ones. Each mode has its own endpoints; neither key can see the other's.

secret.description: Raw signing secret, shown once. Save it; it cannot be recovered. Use it to verify the X-Distyra-Signature header on incoming deliveries.

patch.summary: Update a webhook endpoint (url, events, status)
patch.description:
Partial update. Provide any subset of url, events, status. `events` fully replaces the subscription list. Setting status=active clears the failure counter and re-enables an auto-disabled endpoint. The signing secret is unchanged. Use rotate_secret for that.

**Required scope:** `webhooks:write`.

url.description: New HTTPS URL. Plain HTTP rejected.

events.description: Replacement event subscription list (full replace, not merge).

status.description: Set 'disabled' to pause deliveries, 'active' to resume (also clears the failure counter).

livemode.description: false for an endpoint created with a test key. It receives events about test-mode activity only, and a live endpoint only live ones. Each mode has its own endpoints; neither key can see the other's.

post.summary: Generate a new signing secret for an existing endpoint
post.description:
The new secret takes effect immediately on the next delivery. Customers must update their verifier before this call lands; rotate in a maintenance window or accept brief signature mismatches during the cutover.

**Required scope:** `webhooks:write`.

livemode.description: false for an endpoint created with a test key. It receives events about test-mode activity only, and a live endpoint only live ones. Each mode has its own endpoints; neither key can see the other's.

secret.description: Raw signing secret, shown once. Save it; it cannot be recovered. Use it to verify the X-Distyra-Signature header on incoming deliveries.

get.summary: List banks (ASPSPs) available for a country
get.description:
The banks we can open a connection to in a given country, for the given PSU type. Pass a name from this list verbatim as `aspsp_name` on POST /v1/connect/connections: a loose match is refused rather than guessed at.

**Required scope:** `connect:read`.

max_consent_days.description: How long this bank will keep a consent valid, in days. Connect requests exactly this for your own and end-user connections, so it is how long before the account holder must re-authorise. Null when the bank publishes no maximum, in which case 90 days is requested. Measured across the EEA on 2026-09-04, almost every bank permits 180.

psu_types.description: Which account holder types this bank supports (`business`, `personal`, or both).

data_caveats.description: Present only when we know something specific about what this bank does not send, so you can set expectations before an account holder picks it. Absent is not a grade: it covers both banks that send everything and banks we hold no evidence about, and the two should not be presented the same way. Nothing here ranks banks against each other. These describe what a connector has sent in the past, sometimes only a few dozen transactions, rather than the account being connected, so treat them as context worth surfacing rather than a reason to steer somebody away from their own bank.

no_transaction_type.description: This bank has not sent a transaction code or a description in the traffic we have seen from it, so expect `transaction_type` to be null. Nothing to retry: it changes if the bank starts sending it.

sparse_counterparty_name.description: This bank has typically left the counterparty name off a meaningful share of entries. Those fall back to whatever reference text the bank sends, which is weaker to identify a merchant from than a payee name, so expect more of them to come back unresolved.

no_counterparty_text.description: Stronger than `sparse_counterparty_name` and never sent alongside it. This bank has sent neither a counterparty name nor remittance text on a meaningful share of entries, so expect some rows to carry no text at all: a date, an amount and nothing to identify. Those cannot be enriched by anyone.

beta.description: Enable Banking marks this connector **beta**. It is the provider's own maturity marker, passed through unchanged, and it is a disclosure rather than a prediction: beta connectors do work and some non-beta ones fail. What it tells you is that this connector has had less exposure than a generally available one, so when choosing between two banks for a first integration, prefer the one without this flag. Absent means not marked beta. Measured on the live registry 2026-10-01: 96% of Italian connectors carry it, 70% of French and 53% of Spanish, so in some countries almost every choice carries it.

observed_through.description: The newest traffic behind the three sparseness flags above, as a date. Present whenever any of them is, absent otherwise, and it does **not** describe `beta`, which comes from the live connector record rather than from observed traffic. Read it as a weight on the claim rather than as decoration: these flags come from a periodic sample of what connectors have sent, so a flag dated some months back may describe a bank that has since started sending the field. The strongest flag is the one most exposed to this, because `no_transaction_type` rests on having seen no code at all, and never having observed one is not the same as the bank not sending one. If a date here is old and the distinction matters to you, ask us to re-check that bank rather than designing around it.

bank_error_kind.description: When the bank refused the request and we can say how. `rate_limited`: the bank is limiting requests for this connection; wait a few minutes before trying again, because retrying sooner usually extends the limit. `bank_timeout`: the bank did not answer in time. `bank_error`: the bank answered with an error of its own. `account_not_accessible`: the bank says the account holder no longer has access to this account, or it does not exist. `action_required`: the bank needs the account holder to do something at the bank before it will answer. Absent when the failure was not one of these. New values may be added, so treat an unknown one like an absent one.

post.summary: Open a bank connection (returns the authorization URL)
post.description:
Opens a PSD2/AIS connection and returns the bank authorization URL to send the account holder to. The connection is `pending` until they finish authorizing at their bank, at which point it flips to `active` and a `connect.connection.activated` webhook fires. `aspsp_name` must be an exact name from GET /v1/connect/aspsps.

**Required scope:** `connect:write`.

aspsp_name.description: Bank name; resolved to the canonical Enable Banking ASPSP name.

applicant_ref.description:
Your reference for the underwriting applicant/deal. Sending it selects `mode: 'applicant'` and needs an Underwriting subscription. Must be non-empty when present.

This names a deal, not a person you do business with. If you are connecting the accounts of users of your own product, leave this out and send `mode: 'end_user'` with `external_ref` instead; if the accounts are your organization’s own, leave both out. It is the only field here that reads like a customer id, which is why it is the one most often reached for by mistake.

Use a pseudonymous id, meaningful only inside your own systems. Do not put a name, email address or other directly identifying detail here: we cannot tell one from the other, we store what you send, and you are the controller for it. We erase it when your organization is deleted, and billing records reference the connection rather than this value so the erasure holds.

external_ref.description:
Your own stable id for this connection (e.g. your user or account id). Unlike the connection id, it survives reconsent: pass the same value when a customer re-authorizes and key your integration off it. Echoed in list responses and every connect.connection.* webhook.

Use a pseudonymous id, meaningful only inside your own systems. Do not put a name, email address or other directly identifying detail here: we cannot tell one from the other, we store what you send, and you are the controller for it. We erase it when your organization is deleted, and billing records reference the connection rather than this value so the erasure holds.

mode.description:
Whose account this is. `own` (your organization's own, the default), `applicant` (your underwriting applicant's, equivalent to sending applicant_ref), or `end_user` (a user of an application you offer). Omit and we infer it from applicant_ref, which is what every existing integration does. Send it explicitly for `end_user`: nothing else distinguishes a user of your product from an account you hold yourself, and the difference decides the consent window, the reconsent email and who we say the account belongs to.

If a mode is not available for your organization, the request is refused with `connect_mode_unavailable`.

When business verification is required for live `end_user` connections, an unverified organization is refused with `business_verification_required`, or `business_verification_pending` while a check is still running. You verify once in the portal under Connect.

return_url.description: Where to send the account holder after consent. Defaults to a Distyra-hosted page. Required when `mode` is `end_user`: that person is inside your product and must be returned to it, not left on a page of ours telling them to close the window.

psu_type.description: Whether the account holder is a business or a private individual. Must match the `psu_type` you listed the bank under in GET /v1/connect/aspsps: banks are registered per type and a name from the personal list is not resolvable as a business one. Sole traders and freelancers routinely run a business on a personal account, so this is not a statement about who your customer is, it is which registration to use. Defaults to `business`.

parameters.name: psu-ip-address
parameters.description: Your end user's IP, when one is waiting on this call. Send with `Psu-User-Agent`; both or neither. Some banks require both to start an authorization at all.

parameters.name: psu-user-agent
parameters.description: Your end user's browser User-Agent. Send with `Psu-Ip-Address`; both or neither. Some banks require both to start an authorization at all.

authorization_url.description: Redirect the applicant here to complete SCA at their bank.

get.summary: List your bank connections
get.description:
Your organization's connections, newest first. Metadata only: no transaction data is stored behind a connection, so nothing here carries amounts or dates.

Test and live are separate: a test key lists the sandbox connections created with test keys, and a live key lists live connections. The same holds for every route that reads or ends a connection by id, where a connection of the other mode answers 404 with a detail naming the key that reads it.

Page with `cursor`: pass the `next_cursor` from the previous response until it comes back null. The cursor is a position in the result, not an offset, so connections created while you page do not shift rows onto a page you have already read.

Filter by `external_ref` to find the connections for one of your own users. Note that external_ref is a history key, not a unique one: re-authorizing mints a new connection carrying the same reference, so a lookup can return several rows and the first is the current one.

Filter by `expires_before` (with `status=active`) to find the connections that need reconnecting. The `connect.connection.reconsent_required` webhook pushes the same signal one connection at a time and is the better fit for reacting to a lapse; this is for rendering state and for catching up after missed deliveries.

**Required scope:** `connect:read`.

parameters.name: external_ref
parameters.description: Return only connections carrying this reference of yours, newest first.

parameters.name: expires_before
parameters.description: Return only connections whose bank consent lapses before this instant. Combine with `status=active` to answer "which of my connections need reconnecting", which is otherwise only knowable by paging every row and comparing `consent_expires_at` yourself. Connections with no consent expiry (pending, or never activated) are excluded. An instant rather than a number of days, so your clock and ours cannot disagree about where the window ends.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100, which is what this endpoint always returned.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from your previous response.

mode.description: Which access mode this connection is: `own` (your organization's own accounts), `applicant` (your underwriting applicant's), or `end_user` (the end user of an application you offer). Set at creation and never inferred.

failure_reason.description: Why an attempt failed. **Present only when `status` is `error`**, and absent otherwise rather than null, because on a connection that did not fail the question does not apply. The four values need **different things from you**, which is the reason this field exists at all: `psu_denied`, the account holder declined or cancelled at their own bank, so invite them again; `no_code`, the bank returned them to us without an authorization code, which usually means they abandoned the screen, so invite them again; `code_exchange_failed`, our exchange with the bank failed after they authorized, which is ours to fix, so retry later rather than asking them again; `persist_failed`, the bank authorized and we could not store the result, also ours. **Treat this as an open enum**: switch on the values you know and have a default branch, because a new reason ships in `/v1` without a version bump. Nothing the bank or our provider said is published here, only our own verdict.

failure_kind.description: A more specific account of why an attempt failed, alongside `failure_reason`. **Present only when `status` is `error`.** `failure_reason` is unchanged; this adds what it cannot say, where an error the bank returned during authorization is concerned: `bank_error`, the bank reported a problem of its own while the account holder was authorizing, which they did not cause, so invite them again a little later; `authorization_rejected`, the bank refused our authorization request as we made it, which is ours to fix, so contact us rather than asking them again; `authorization_failed`, the bank ended the attempt with an error we do not recognise, which can happen when the bank page is left open too long, so invite them again and tell us if it repeats; `psu_denied`, the account holder declined or cancelled. Each of those four arrives with `failure_reason: psu_denied`. For every other failure this repeats `failure_reason`. **An open enum**: switch on the values you know and keep a default branch.

anyOf.description: A kind added after your client was generated. Handle it in your default branch.

data_caveats.description: What this bank does not send, when we know something specific about it. Same field and same meaning as on GET /v1/connect/aspsps, repeated here so it is available after the connection is open and not only while choosing. Absent is not a grade.

no_transaction_type.description: This bank has not sent a transaction code or a description in the traffic we have seen from it, so expect `transaction_type` to be null. Nothing to retry: it changes if the bank starts sending it.

sparse_counterparty_name.description: This bank has typically left the counterparty name off a meaningful share of entries. Those fall back to whatever reference text the bank sends, which is weaker to identify a merchant from than a payee name, so expect more of them to come back unresolved.

no_counterparty_text.description: Stronger than `sparse_counterparty_name` and never sent alongside it. This bank has sent neither a counterparty name nor remittance text on a meaningful share of entries, so expect some rows to carry no text at all: a date, an amount and nothing to identify. Those cannot be enriched by anyone.

observed_through.description: The newest traffic behind the three sparseness flags above, as a date. Present whenever any of them is, absent otherwise, and it does **not** describe `beta`, which comes from the live connector record rather than from observed traffic. Read it as a weight on the claim rather than as decoration: these flags come from a periodic sample of what connectors have sent, so a flag dated some months back may describe a bank that has since started sending the field. The strongest flag is the one most exposed to this, because `no_transaction_type` rests on having seen no code at all, and never having observed one is not the same as the bank not sending one. If a date here is old and the distinction matters to you, ask us to re-check that bank rather than designing around it.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Null when this is the last page. A full page with a null cursor is the normal end of a list whose size is an exact multiple of your limit.

next_step.description: Present only when your organization has no connections at all and no filter or cursor was sent. Says how to create the first one. Absent on every other response, including an empty page from a filter.

If a date here is old and the distinction matters to you, ask us to re-check that bank rather than designing around it.

delete.description:
Ends the connection and withdraws the bank consent behind it. Idempotent: revoking an already-revoked connection succeeds. An `own` or `end_user` connection is billed a month at a time from the day it activated, not by calendar month. Revoking stops the next month being charged; the month already started is not refunded.

**Cleaning up attempts that never finished.** Send `expected_status=pending` and the connection is ended only while it is still pending. If the account holder finished authorizing first, the call answers 409 `connection_not_pending` and changes nothing, so an automated sweep cannot end a connection that has just succeeded. Use it for that sweep, because a hosted link bounds only when a flow may **start**, not when it may finish: an authorization begun before the link expired can still complete after it, so the link's `expires_at` is not a safe cleanup threshold on its own. Measure age from the connection's `created_at`, which is when the authorization began, instead.

**Required scope:** `connect:write`.

parameters.name: expected_status
parameters.description: Precondition. With `pending`, revoke only while the connection is still pending: 409 if the account holder has already authorized (`active`), or did and the consent has since lapsed (`expired`). A connection that is already `revoked`, or that failed at the bank (`error`), answers 204, so retrying a call that succeeded is safe. Omit to revoke whatever state the connection is in.

get.summary: List the accounts on a connection
get.description:
The accounts the account holder authorized on this connection. Served from our own metadata, so it answers even when the bank is unreachable; live balances are best-effort and each account reports `balance_known` accordingly. With `allow_stored=true`, a call in the five minutes after a fetch for the connection failed at the bank returns the accounts without live balances and does not use a fetch from the daily allowance. The IBAN is returned masked (`iban_masked`). The full value is seen once, during the authorization exchange, and is not stored.

`account_id` identifies an account **on this connection only**. The bank issues a new one at every authorization, so an account the same holder re-authorizes comes back under a different `account_id`. To match it against one you already hold, compare `(iban_masked, currency)` within the connection, and treat that as a heuristic: `iban_masked` is four characters, and this API publishes no stable account key.

This call reaches the bank, so it draws on the same daily allowance as GET /v1/connect/connections/{id}/transactions and answers the same 429 when it is spent. One live balance call is made per account. The allowance belongs to the connection, not to a route, so four fetches here and four there is still four in total. As on the transactions endpoint, sending `Psu-Ip-Address` and `Psu-User-Agent` for an end user who is actually on screen exempts the call.

**Required scope:** `connect:read`.

parameters.name: allow_stored
parameters.description: When `true`, and a fetch for this connection failed at the bank in the last five minutes, answer from the account details we hold, without live balances and without using a fetch from the daily allowance. Each account then reads `balance_known: false`. Has no effect on a fetch made while your user is on screen. When omitted or `false`, the call reaches the bank as it always has.

parameters.name: psu-ip-address
parameters.description: Your end user's IP, when one is waiting on this call. Send with `Psu-User-Agent`; both or neither.

parameters.name: psu-user-agent
parameters.description: Your end user's browser User-Agent. Send with `Psu-Ip-Address`; both or neither.

account_id.description: The bank's identifier for this account **on this connection only**, and what `/transactions` tags each entry with. **Not stable across re-authorization:** the bank issues a new one every time the account holder authorizes, so the same account comes back under a different `account_id` on the next connection. To recognise an account across connections, match on `(iban_masked, currency)` within the connection, which names its own bank. The currency half is load-bearing, not decoration: some banks return several currency accounts behind a **single** shared IBAN, so matching on the IBAN alone collapses them into a single account. `iban_masked` is the last four characters, so this is a heuristic and not an identity: we publish no stable account key today, and null `iban_masked` leaves nothing to match on.

uid.description: The same value as `account_id`, byte for byte. Kept for callers written against the earlier field name; prefer `account_id`.

iban_masked.description: Last four characters of the IBAN, masked for display (e.g. `•••• 1234`). The full IBAN is returned only once, in the authorization exchange, and is not stored. Null when the bank supplied no IBAN for that account, in which case re-authorizing changes nothing. It can also be null on a connection authorized before 2026-08-28, or before 2026-10-12 at a bank that sends the IBAN only among its other account identifiers; re-authorizing fills those in. Do not treat null as a prompt to re-authorize on its own.

account_type.description: Who holds the account, as the bank reports it: `business` or `personal`. Omitted when the bank does not say. This is the holder type, not the kind of account; see `cash_account_type` for current, savings or card.

cash_account_type.description: The kind of account, as the ISO 20022 code the bank reports: `CACC` current account, `SVGS` savings, `CARD` card account, `LOAN` loan, `CASH` cash account, `OTHR` anything else. Captured when the account holder authorizes the connection, because banks provide it only then. Null for connections authorized before this field was added in September 2026 (re-authorizing fills it in) and when the bank sends no recognised code.

balance.description: One balance per account, chosen for you: the available balance when the bank sends one, otherwise the closing booked balance, otherwise the first balance the bank lists. Kept as it has always been. To read the booked and the available balance separately, use `balance_booked` and `balance_available`.

balance_booked.description: The booked balance: what the bank has booked to the account, without pending entries. Taken from the interim booked balance (`ITBD`, calculated during the day) when the bank sends one, otherwise the closing booked balance (`CLBD`, at the end of the bank's last reporting period); `balance_type` says which. Null when the bank sends neither, or when balances could not be read. Comes from the same bank call as `balance`, so it costs nothing extra.

currency.description: The currency the bank gave for this balance. Null if it gave none.

balance_type.description: The ISO 20022 balance type this figure was taken from.

balance_available.description: The available balance: what the bank reports as available to spend. Taken from the interim available balance (`ITAV`, calculated during the day) when the bank sends one, otherwise the closing available balance (`CLAV`); `balance_type` says which. Null when the bank sends neither, or when balances could not be read. Comes from the same bank call as `balance`, so it costs nothing extra.

currency.description: The currency the bank gave for this balance. Null if it gave none.

balance_type.description: The ISO 20022 balance type this figure was taken from.

get.summary: Account-holder identity for a connection (ownership verification)
get.description:
Returns the account holder name the bank reports for each account. Pass applicant_name to get a token-match verdict (match / partial / no_match) per account, to confirm an account belongs to your applicant. Holder names are provided by the bank and vary in format; use the verdict as a confirmation signal.

**Required scope:** `connect:read`.

parameters.name: applicant_name
parameters.description: Name to match holders against.

iban_masked.description: Last four characters of the IBAN, masked for display (e.g. `•••• 1234`). The full IBAN is returned only once, in the authorization exchange, and is not stored. Null when the bank supplied no IBAN for that account, in which case re-authorizing changes nothing. It can also be null on a connection authorized before 2026-08-28, or before 2026-10-12 at a bank that sends the IBAN only among its other account identifiers; re-authorizing fills those in. Do not treat null as a prompt to re-authorize on its own.

account_type.description: Who holds the account, as the bank reports it: `business` or `personal`. Omitted when the bank does not say. This is the holder type, not the kind of account; see `cash_account_type` for current, savings or card.

cash_account_type.description: The kind of account, as the ISO 20022 code the bank reports: `CACC` current account, `SVGS` savings, `CARD` card account, `LOAN` loan, `CASH` cash account, `OTHR` anything else. Captured when the account holder authorizes the connection, because banks provide it only then. Null for connections authorized before this field was added in September 2026 (re-authorizing fills it in) and when the bank sends no recognised code.
